summary: Minimum angle per circle fragment in degrees; caps 360/$fa fragments. Used only when $fn == 0.

params.name: value
params.desc: Degrees per fragment. Values below 0.01 are clamped to 0.01 with a WARNING.

semantics: One of the two adaptive tessellation knobs. When $fn==0, fragments = ceil(max(min(360/$fa, 2*PI*r/$fs), 5)): $fa contributes the angular cap 360/$fa, $fs contributes the arc-length cap, and whichever demands FEWER fragments wins the min(), with an absolute floor of 5 fragments. Dynamically scoped; settable per call or via -D.
edge_cases: $fa < 0.01 (including 0 and negatives) is clamped to 0.01 and emits a WARNING approximately '$fa too small - clamping to 0.01'. VERIFY: exact message text and whether the warning fires at assignment time or at first use.
Default 12 gives 360/12 = 30 fragments for large radii (when $fs is not the binding constraint).
Ignored entirely whenever $fn > 0 in scope — no warning about the shadowed value.
The min() with the $fs term means lowering $fa alone does NOT increase fragments if $fs already binds (common confusion; both must be lowered for small parts).
Absolute minimum of 5 fragments applies on this path (contrast: the $fn path floors at 3).
Radius below GRID_FINE (2^-20) short-circuits to 3 fragments before $fa is consulted.
Non-numeric $fa: VERIFY behavior (expected: type error/warning and fallback to default) — pin via oracle.
Consumers identical to $fn: circle, sphere, cylinder(max r), rotate_extrude (angle-scaled), offset(r), text, linear_extrude twist slices default.
impl_notes: Clamp-warning text and trigger point are observable surface (users run --hardwarnings). Probe with $fa=0.001 and capture the exact console line. The min/max/ceil composition must match bit-for-bit at boundary radii; test radii where 360/$fa == 2*PI*r/$fs exactly.

name: $fs
summary: Minimum fragment size (arc length in model units); caps 2*PI*r/$fs fragments. Used only when $fn == 0.

params.name: value
params.desc: Minimum arc length per fragment. Values below 0.01 are clamped to 0.01 with a WARNING.

semantics: Partner knob to $fa in the adaptive formula ceil(max(min(360/$fa, 2*PI*r/$fs), 5)). For small radii the $fs term is small, the min() picks it, and the floor of 5 fragments takes over — this is why tiny circles render as pentagons by default. Dynamically scoped; settable per call or via -D.
edge_cases: $fs < 0.01 clamped to 0.01 with WARNING approximately '$fs too small - clamping to 0.01'. VERIFY exact text and trigger point.
Default $fs=2 makes a default circle(r=1) hit the 5-fragment floor (2*PI*1/2 ~= 3.14 < 5): a default tiny circle is a pentagon — widely observed behavior, must reproduce.
Ignored when $fn > 0.
The formula uses arc length (2*PI*r/$fs), not chord length — do not 'improve' to chords.
For cylinder the r in the formula is max(r1,r2); a cone with r1=10,r2=0 tessellates like r=10.
r < GRID_FINE short-circuits to 3 fragments before $fs is consulted.
VERIFY: offset(r=x) feeds |x| as the radius into the formula for corner-rounding fragments — pin via oracle.
Warning set (clamped $fa/$fs) counts toward --hardwarnings fatality.
impl_notes: Golden-test the 5-fragment floor with circle(r=1) defaults and the crossover radius where $fa starts binding (r where 2*PI*r/$fs > 360/$fa, i.e. r > 30*2/(2*PI) ~= 9.549 at defaults). Vertex counts in exported STL/CSG are the oracle.

name: $t
summary: Animation time, nominally in [0,1); driven by the GUI animation panel (FPS x Steps) or set externally; models read it to parameterize animated geometry.

params.name: value
params.desc: Current animation fraction. Frame k of an n-step animation runs with $t = k/n.

semantics: Outside animation $t is 0. With the GUI animation panel active, the model is re-evaluated repeatedly with $t stepping through k/Steps; 'Dump Pictures' writes a PNG per frame. Ordinary dynamic-scoping rules apply: a script may assign $t itself (top-level assignment overrides the environment-provided value under last-write-wins), and may pass $t=x into calls.
edge_cases: $t never reaches 1.0 from the GUI stepper ($t = frame/steps, frames 0..steps-1); scripts written for looping animations rely on [0,1) semantics.
VERIFY: a top-level '$t = 0.25;' in the script overrides the GUI/CLI-provided value for the whole run (last-write-wins over the injected outer value) — pin precedence via oracle.
CLI: --animate N is NEW in 2021.01 (pre-2021 releases required external -D '$t=...' looping); the frame number is appended to the -o output filename, 5-digit zero-padded.
-D '$t=0.5' works like any -D injection and wins over in-file assignment.
Reading $t when nothing set it yields 0, not undef — the default is a real binding in the outermost scope.
Geometry caching interacts: each distinct $t value forces re-evaluation of $t-dependent subtrees; $t-independent subtrees stay cached (performance surface, not semantics).
Non-numeric assignment is not special-cased: $t = "x" simply flows to whatever reads it, with normal type-mismatch warnings downstream.

The GUI animation panel and CLI --animate N drive $t through N frames of k/N (0..1), writing a frame%05d.png sequence; $t is 0 in ordinary (non-animated) runs. FPS/steps are GUI state, not language state.
example:
$vpr = [60, 0, 360 * $t]; // spinning camera
rotate([0, 0, 360 * $t]) cube([10, 2, 2], center = true);
impl_notes: Semantics are trivial (a pre-bound outer variable); the app decides how it is driven. Expose it in your MCP/CLI as an injectable binding. Only precedence vs in-file assignment needs an oracle probe.

name: $vpr
summary: Viewport/camera rotation in degrees. Reading returns the live GUI camera; top-level assignment moves the camera after each preview.

params.name: value
params.desc: Euler rotation of the viewport in degrees, [x, y, z].

semantics: One of the viewport specials ($vpr/$vpt/$vpd/$vpf). In the GUI, reads reflect the camera state at evaluation time (so echo($vpr) tracks user orbiting after the recompile). A TOP-LEVEL assignment sets the camera once the preview compile finishes — combined with $t this scripts camera animation paths. In CLI runs the values reflect --camera arguments, or the defaults when none given.
edge_cases: Default [55, 0, 25] — the standard startup view; CLI exports without --camera evaluate with the defaults.
Assignments below top level do NOT move the camera; VERIFY: such an assignment still creates an ordinary dynamically-scoped variable readable in that subtree — pin via oracle.

The GUI writes the current camera into the variables BEFORE evaluation, so a script that both reads and assigns $vpr sees the pre-assignment (live) value in expressions evaluated before its own assignment position; last-write-wins ordering applies within the top scope. VERIFY exact read-vs-assign interleaving.
--camera=tx,ty,tz,rx,ry,rz,dist maps rx,ry,rz to $vpr; the alternate --camera=eyex,...,centerx,... form is converted to the rotational model. VERIFY converted values as read back.
Values are plain numbers in a 3-vector; nothing normalizes angles (e.g. 385 stays 385 when read back within the same evaluation; the GUI may normalize between frames — VERIFY).
Animation: assigning $vpr from $t is the documented camera-path idiom and must re-apply per frame.
In 2015.03..2019.05 era these existed with same defaults; $vpf joined in 2021.01.
impl_notes: For a headless/always-exact reimplementation: bind defaults, honor CLI camera injection, honor top-level assignment as 'camera request' output. The GUI live-read behavior only needs emulating if you build an interactive viewer; document your choice.

name: $vpt
summary: Viewport translation (camera look-at point). Read = live camera; top-level assignment repositions after preview.

params.name: value
params.desc: Camera target translation vector.

semantics: Same read/assign model as $vpr: reads reflect current camera, top-level assignments take effect after the compile; CLI --camera's tx,ty,tz component populates it.
edge_cases: Default [0,0,0].
Non-top-level assignment does not affect the camera (ordinary $-variable otherwise).
GUI pan updates the value between evaluations; echo($vpt) after panning shows the new center on recompile.
--viewall/--autocenter CLI options recompute the camera; VERIFY what $vpt reads as in that case (the pre-adjustment value is expected, since adjustment happens after evaluation).
Assigning a wrong-shaped value (scalar, 2-vector): VERIFY behavior — expected: camera assignment ignored, possibly warning; the variable still holds the value for readers.
impl_notes: Same as $vpr: treat as camera I/O channel; oracle-probe only if you claim GUI parity.

name: $vpd
summary: Viewport camera distance. Read = live camera; top-level assignment sets zoom after preview.

params.name: value
params.desc: Distance from camera to the $vpt target.

semantics: Same model as $vpr/$vpt. The dist component of --camera populates it in CLI runs.
edge_cases: Default 140.
Zooming in the GUI changes the value read on the next recompile.
$vpd = 0 or negative: VERIFY — expected degenerate camera accepted or clamped by the viewer; the language variable itself stores any number.
With --projection=ortho the distance still controls the ortho scale (viewer behavior).
impl_notes: Trivial; document viewer behavior for degenerate values rather than oracling them unless you promise GUI parity.

name: $vpf
summary: Viewport camera field-of-view in degrees. NEW in 2021.01; same live-read/top-level-assign model as the other $vp* variables.

params.name: value
params.desc: Vertical field of view in degrees for the perspective camera.

semantics: Completes the camera quartet. Read returns the GUI camera FOV; top-level assignment applies after preview. Not present in 2019.05 and earlier.
edge_cases: Default 22.5 degrees.
On pre-2021.01 versions reading $vpf is an unknown variable (undef; VERIFY whether the unknown-$-variable warning fires) — feature-test material for scripts.
FOV <= 0 or >= 180: VERIFY clamping in the viewer.
Ignored under orthographic projection (viewer behavior), but the variable still reads/writes normally.
impl_notes: Report it if you pin version() to 2021.01 — libraries may probe it. Trivial otherwise.

name: $children
signature: $children  // integer, set by the module-call mechanism
summary: Number of child instantiations passed to the currently executing module; 0 at top level and for childless calls.
semantics: Automatically bound on every module invocation to the count of children at the call site, before the body runs. Used to guard children(i) indexing and to loop 'for (i = [0:1:$children-1]) children(i);'. Dynamically scoped like all specials: nested module calls each rebind it; function calls made from the body see the module's value.
edge_cases: Top level: $children is 0 (the implicit root group has no 'passed' children in the user-visible sense). VERIFY: 0 vs unknown-variable at top level — pin via oracle.
A single child without braces counts as 1; a braced block 'm(){a();b();}' counts each statement: 2; an empty block {} gives 0.
A for-loop as a child counts as ONE child (the loop is a single group node), not one per iteration — classic trap; children([0:$children-1]) over a for-child sees 1.
if/else as a child likewise counts as 1 regardless of which branch is taken (VERIFY: including a false-with-no-else if, which yields an empty group child).
Assigning $children yourself is legal syntax (any $-var is assignable) but is immediately shadowed at the next module call; scripts doing this get self-inflicted confusion, not an error.
children(i) with i outside 0..$children-1 warns/errors (message owned by children(); see modules category).
$children inside a function called from the module body resolves dynamically to the calling module's count.
Range guard idiom 'if ($children > 1)' is common in libraries (e.g. conditional union wrappers) — must be exact.
example:
module pair() { children(0); translate([20, 0, 0]) children($children - 1); }
pair() { cube(5); sphere(3); } // echo($children) inside would print 2
since: pre-2015.03 (predates 2014.03 — existed with legacy child(); 2014.03 fixed a dynamic-scoping bug and added children()/parent_module()/$parent_modules)
impl_notes: Bind it in the module-call frame alongside the children list; ensure for/if children count as single group nodes. Oracle-probe top-level read and the for-as-one-child case.

name: $preview
signature: $preview  // boolean, set by the evaluation mode
summary: true during F5/OpenCSG preview (and PNG export with --preview); false during F6 render and CLI mesh/2D exports. The standard knob for preview-speed vs render-quality tradeoffs.
semantics: Bound by the application before evaluation: GUI F5 -> true; GUI F6 -> false; CLI mesh/2D export (-o model.stl etc.) -> false; CLI PNG with --preview (or default PNG behavior) -> true; CLI PNG with --render -> false. Idioms: '$fn = $preview ? 24 : 120;', skipping minkowski()/expensive ops in preview, preview-only annotations.
edge_cases: Introduced 2019.05; on older versions reading it warns unknown-variable and yields undef — libraries feature-test with 'is_undef($preview) ? ... '.
CLI PNG default is preview mode, so $preview==true for plain '-o out.png'; --render flips it to false. VERIFY: '--preview=throwntogether' also true.

-D '$preview=true' injects a trailing top-level assignment that overrides the mode-provided value under last-write-wins — users do this to force preview-quality geometry in exports. VERIFY precedence via oracle.
An in-file top-level '$preview = false;' similarly overrides for the whole run. VERIFY.
It is an ordinary boolean binding, not magic: passing $preview=true into a subtree call re-binds it dynamically for that subtree only — legal and occasionally used.
Consistency requirement: %/# modifier visibility, color() visibility, and $preview must all agree with whichever mode your app claims to be in, or scripts render inconsistently.
impl_notes: Decide your app's preview story first, then set this coherently everywhere (including your PNG/thumbnail paths). It is just an outer-scope binding; only the override precedence needs pinning.

name: user-defined $-variables and dynamic scoping
summary: Every $-prefixed identifier — built-in or invented — is dynamically scoped down the instantiation/call stack, and any call may pass any $name=value as an undeclared named argument.
semantics: Setting a $-variable in a scope makes it visible to ALL descendant module instantiations and function calls made while that scope is active (dynamic scoping), unlike plain variables (lexical). Passing $foo=1 as a named argument to any module or function is always accepted without the callee declaring $foo, never triggers the unknown-named-argument warning, and binds $foo for the callee's entire dynamic extent. children() bodies evaluate in the CALLER's lexical scope but under the INSTANTIATING module's current $-environment — the mechanism behind '$fn propagates into children'. Function literals capture their lexical environment for plain names but resolve $-names dynamically at call time.
edge_cases: Reading a never-set $-variable yields undef. VERIFY: whether 2021.01 emits the 'unknown variable' WARNING for unset $-variables (plain variables definitely warn; the seed believes $-vars do not) — pin via oracle; libraries read optional flags like $slop expecting silence.
Unknown named NON-$ arguments warn ('unknown parameter') and are ignored; $-named arguments are silently accepted everywhere — this asymmetry is load-bearing for BOSL2.

A module parameter literally named with $ (module m($x=1)) is legal: it declares a default for the special and callers may omit it; the default applies only if no dynamic value is inherited? VERIFY exact precedence of declared-default vs inherited dynamic value.
for ($i = [0:2]) is legal; the loop variable is then dynamically scoped into calls made from the body. VERIFY.
let($fn=12) expr scopes the special for the expression's dynamic extent (including functions it calls).
Modifier: assignments to $-vars inside a block do not leak out (scoping rules for blocks still apply); dynamic means 'flows into calls', not 'flows back up'.
echo($foo=5) both binds and prints 'VERIFY: whether the named $-arg is printed like a normal named arg ($foo = 5) — pin.'
is_undef($never_set) suppresses any warning (same guard behavior as plain variables).
Cost warning: every function call must consult the dynamic chain for $-lookups; naive deep-copy of $-environments per call is a known performance trap.
impl_notes: Implement as a parallel dynamic environment (linked frames) threaded through module instantiation, function application, AND children() re-instantiation. Getting children()'s hybrid scoping wrong is the number-one library breaker; write oracle tests mixing lexical capture and $-inheritance through children().

name: include
summary: Lexical inclusion of another .scad file: its top-level variables, module/function definitions, AND geometry all take effect in the including scope, as if pasted — with the quirk that main-file assignments override included ones.

params.name: path
params.desc: Angle-bracket file path; no quotes, spaces allowed, everything up to '>' is the path; no escape mechanism, so '>' cannot appear in a filename.

semantics: Processed at parse time. The included file's statements execute in the including file's scope: geometry is instantiated, definitions are registered, and top-level assignments join the includer's top-level scope. Since 2019.05, assignments in the MAIN file override same-name assignments from included files REGARDLESS of textual order — this is the documented pattern for overriding library defaults (include <lib.scad> then 'width = 5;' wins even though lib assigned later-in-merged-order; and 'width = 5;' before the include also wins). Nested includes resolve their paths relative to the file containing the directive. No include guards exist: including a file twice re-executes it (duplicate geometry, duplicate-definition warnings).
edge_cases: Missing file: WARNING approximately "Can't open include file 'x.scad'." and evaluation continues with the file simply absent. VERIFY exact text.
Double inclusion duplicates geometry and re-registers definitions; duplicate definitions in one scope warn with last-one-wins. Observable warning surface.

Main-file-overrides-included is a 2019.05 behavior change; before that, plain last-write-wins textual order governed. Pin to the 2019.05+ rule for the 2021.01 baseline. VERIFY: whether includes nested two deep also lose to the main file (expected: any included assignment loses to a main-file assignment; between two included files, VERIFY which wins — expected later include wins).

include may appear inside a module body or block (it is lexical); the included content then lives in that inner scope. VERIFY: officially documented for use only as top-level-restricted; include's in-block legality and exact scoping must be pinned.
Recursive/self include: VERIFY whether 2021.01 detects the cycle (expected: it errors or hangs — pin the observed behavior and prefer a clean cycle error with matching text if any).
No semicolon after the directive; VERIFY whether a trailing ';' parses (as an error or tolerated).
Path search order on non-relative hits: including file's directory, then OPENSCADPATH entries, then the user library folder, then bundled installation libraries (see search-path entry).
-D and Customizer overrides beat included-file assignments (they inject after everything in the main scope).
Customizer does NOT surface parameters from included files (main file only).
The included file's geometry participates in the implicit union of the including scope at the position of the directive.
Windows path separators and case-sensitivity follow the host filesystem; write tests with forward slashes only for portability.
impl_notes: Implement as parse-time file splicing plus the special main-scope assignment precedence (tag assignments with their file-of-origin; main-file tags outrank). Oracle-probe: include-then-assign, assign-then-include, two includes assigning the same name, and double-include warning text.

name: use
summary: Imports ONLY the module and function definitions from another file; the used file's top-level geometry is not instantiated and its top-level variables are private to it.

params.name: path
params.desc: Angle-bracket file path, same lexical rules as include.

semantics: The used file is parsed and its top-level module/function definitions become callable in the using file. Its top-level geometry statements are NOT instantiated. Since 2019.05 its top-level variable assignments ARE evaluated — in the used file's own private scope — so its functions/modules see their own file's constants; those variables are invisible to and NOT overridable by the user (not by assignment, not by -D, not by the Customizer). Parametrize via arguments instead. use must appear at a file's top level.
edge_cases: use inside a block/module is a syntax error. VERIFY exact parser error text.
Pre-2019.05, used-file top-level variables were NOT evaluated (its functions saw undef) — material 2019.05 change; the 2021.01 baseline evaluates them.
Definitions from a use'd file are shadowed by same-name definitions in the using file (local wins). VERIFY precedence and whether a warning fires.

use is not transitive: modules that the used file itself use's are available inside the used file but are NOT re-exported to the user. VERIFY. (include inside a used file IS part of the used file's content and its definitions do carry through.)
Using the same file twice is effectively idempotent. VERIFY: no duplicate-definition warnings expected.
Missing file: WARNING approximately "Can't open library 'x.scad'." — VERIFY text (differs from the include message).
A file both include'd and use'd in one project behaves as both (double execution of definitions; geometry once via the include).
Customizer never shows used-file variables; -D cannot reach them (they are not in the main scope).
The used file's own $-variable reads still resolve dynamically at call time from the CALLER's dynamic environment (e.g. a used module honors the caller's $fn).
Search path identical to include.
impl_notes: Model a used file as a separate top-level scope evaluated once (definitions + private variables, geometry discarded), exporting only its definition table. Keep dynamic $-scoping flowing through the boundary. Oracle-probe: shadowing precedence, transitivity, and both missing-file message texts.

name: library search path resolution
signature: resolution order: <dir of current file> -> OPENSCADPATH entries -> user library folder -> installation libraries
summary: How include/use (and data-file consumers) locate files: current file's directory first, then the OPENSCADPATH environment variable, then the per-user library directory, then bundled libraries.
semantics: Relative paths in include/use are resolved against the directory of the file containing the directive; on miss, each entry of OPENSCADPATH (colon-separated on POSIX, semicolon on Windows) is tried; then the platform user library folder (Windows: My Documents\OpenSCAD\libraries; macOS: ~/Documents/OpenSCAD/libraries; Linux: ~/.local/share/OpenSCAD/libraries); then the installation's bundled libraries (which ship MCAD). First hit wins. Absolute paths bypass the search.
edge_cases: import(), surface(), and text(font=) data files resolve relative to the invoking script's directory; VERIFY whether the library search chain also applies to these data files (seed flags this as unverified; pin per-consumer).
OPENSCADPATH separator is platform-dependent (: vs ;). VERIFY empty-entry handling.
Nested includes/uses resolve relative to THEIR containing file, not the main file — critical for libraries that include their own submodules (BOSL2 does).
MCAD ships in the bundled directory and is GPL/LGPL — a reimplementation must not bundle it without license review; scripts saying include <MCAD/...> rely on the bundled tier existing.
Case sensitivity follows the filesystem; no normalization performed.
A directory (not file) match: VERIFY behavior (expected: open fails, falls through / warns).
The GUI also honors 'Show library folder'; app-level, not language.
impl_notes: Make the search order a documented, testable function; expose the resolved path in verbose logs so users can debug shadowing (a local file silently shadowing a library file is a common support issue). Pin the data-file question with oracle probes before promising it.

name: import
signature: import(file, convexity = 1, layer = <string, DXF only>, dpi = 96 <SVG only>)
summary: Reads an external geometry file and instantiates it as a primitive: STL/OFF/AMF/3MF yield 3D solids; DXF/SVG yield 2D polygons. Format chosen by file extension.

params.name: file
params.desc: Path string, resolved relative to the invoking script's directory. Extension selects the parser (stl, off, amf, 3mf, dxf, svg).

params.name: convexity
params.desc: Preview-only ray-crossing hint for OpenCSG; never affects exported geometry. Default 1.

params.name: layer
params.desc: DXF only: name of the layer to import; omitted imports all layers. VERIFY: ignored silently for other formats.

params.name: dpi
params.desc: SVG only (2019.05+): dots-per-inch used to convert px units to mm; default 96 (1px = 25.4/96 mm).

semantics: Acts exactly like a built-in primitive at its position in the tree: transformable, boolean-composable, modifier-prefixable. Dimensionality is fixed by format (3D mesh formats vs 2D vector formats); mixing an imported 2D shape into a 3D boolean is the standard 'Mixing 2D and 3D objects' error. Meshes are imported as-is for preview; they must be manifold/closed to survive CGAL CSG or F6 render. Curved entities in DXF/SVG are tessellated at import time using the $fn/$fa/$fs in scope at the call.
edge_cases: Unknown/unsupported extension: ERROR approximately 'Unsupported file format while trying to import file' naming the path. VERIFY exact text.
Missing/unreadable file: WARNING and empty geometry; evaluation continues. VERIFY text (approximately "Can't open import file 'x'.").
VERIFY: extension matching is case-insensitive ('.STL' works).
File path resolution: script directory; VERIFY whether library search-path tiers apply (see search-path entry).
convexity is parsed everywhere and ignored by exact pipelines — accept silently.
layer= on a non-DXF import: VERIFY silently ignored vs warning.
dpi < some minimum: VERIFY clamp/warning behavior.
Imported 3D meshes participate in preview un-validated; non-manifold input typically only errors at F6/CSG time (CGAL 'not closed' class errors) — deferred failure is observable behavior.
$fn/$fa/$fs at the call site affect DXF arc/circle and SVG curve tessellation. VERIFY exact application per entity.

Legacy import_stl()/import_dxf()/import_off() still FUNCTION in 2021.01 as deprecated aliases of import(), emitting 'DEPRECATED: The import_stl() module will be removed in future releases. Use import() instead.' (removal came only after 2021.01). dxf_dim()/dxf_cross() remain live separately.
Snapshot-only (2023+): OBJ import, center=true parameter, SVG id=/layer= element selection, 3MF color/material import — absent in 2021.01; flag as opt-in extensions only.

origin=[x,y] and scale= are honored for DXF import in 2021.01 (the legacy DXF pipeline); VERIFY: snapshot additions center= and id=/layer= selection for SVG import — pin exact versions before documenting as contract.
impl_notes: Route by extension into per-format readers (see companion entries). Keep failure modes non-fatal (warn + empty) exactly where OpenSCAD does; scripts rely on continuing. The deferred manifold-validation error timing (preview OK, render fails) must be emulated observably even in an always-exact engine — decide and document where you validate.

name: import: 3D mesh formats (STL, OFF, AMF, 3MF)
summary: The four 3D mesh read formats of 2021.01 and their per-format feature subsets and quirks.
semantics: STL: both ASCII and binary, autodetected. OFF: Geomview text format. AMF: XML mesh format. 3MF: ZIP+XML container read via lib3mf, geometry only in 2021.01. All import as raw triangle/polygon meshes with no unit metadata applied — coordinates are taken as millimeter-equivalent model units.
edge_cases: STL sniffing: a file beginning with 'solid' is tried as ASCII; binary STLs whose 80-byte header happens to start with 'solid' must still load — VERIFY the exact fallback heuristic (ASCII parse failure -> binary reparse) and clone it; this is a real-world file population.
STL binary: little-endian, 80-byte header ignored, uint32 triangle count, 50-byte records; attribute byte count ignored.
STL ASCII: 'solid'/'facet normal'/'outer loop' grammar; stored normals are IGNORED (recomputed from winding). VERIFY.
STL vertices are matched by position to stitch the mesh; VERIFY whether any epsilon/grid snapping applies at import (suspect exact match).
Degenerate (zero-area) triangles: VERIFY dropped vs kept; affects downstream CSG errors.
OFF: header 'OFF', counts line, vertex lines, face lines; per-face color fields tolerated but ignored. VERIFY comment handling ('#').
AMF: reads object/mesh/vertices/triangles; curved-triangle and material/color extensions ignored; multiple objects: VERIFY unioned into one solid vs first-only.
AMF unit attribute: VERIFY honored (scaling) vs ignored in 2021.01.

3MF (2019.05+ read): geometry only in 2021.01 — colors/materials dropped; multiple build items: VERIFY unioned; build transforms: VERIFY applied; units: 3MF is mm-based, VERIFY conversion of other unit declarations.
All four: non-manifold input previews fine, fails at F6/CSG with CGAL-era errors — timing is observable.
OBJ is snapshot-only (2023+); in 2021.01 '.obj' hits the unsupported-format error.
Version asymmetry: AMF EXPORT is 2015.03, but AMF IMPORT only arrived in 2019.05 alongside SVG and 3MF import.
impl_notes: STL sniffing and mesh stitching are the highest-risk items — build a corpus (ASCII, binary, binary-starting-with-'solid', degenerate triangles, unreferenced vertices) and pin behavior. For AMF/3MF pin multi-object and unit handling via oracle before writing the XML/ZIP parsers.

name: import: DXF
summary: 2D import of a limited DXF entity subset: LINE, POLYLINE/LWPOLYLINE, CIRCLE, ARC. Splines are unsupported in 2021.01. Yields 2D polygons at z=0.

params.name: layer
params.desc: Layer name to import; omitted/empty imports entities from all layers. VERIFY default-all behavior.

semantics: Entities are read in file units taken as model units (no unit conversion), connected into closed loops by endpoint matching, and converted to 2D polygon geometry with even-odd style hole nesting as with polygon(). Circles and arcs are tessellated using the $fn/$fa/$fs in scope at the import() call. This DXF reader is the legacy heart of OpenSCAD's original 2D pipeline (dxf_dim/dxf_cross read the same files for metadata).
edge_cases: Unsupported entities (SPLINE, ELLIPSE — VERIFY ellipse, TEXT, DIMENSION geometry, HATCH, INSERT/blocks) are skipped with a WARNING approximately 'Unsupported DXF entity ...' per entity type. VERIFY exact text and which list is warned vs silently ignored.
Open contours (endpoints that do not close a loop) trigger a warning and the open chain is dropped. VERIFY text ('dxf_data: not implemented' / 'open polyline' class messages).
Endpoint matching uses grid quantization to decide coincidence — micro-gap DXFs may or may not close; VERIFY the tolerance and clone it (real-world CAD exports sit right at this edge).
POLYLINE bulge values (arc segments inside polylines): VERIFY supported and tessellation rule.
layer= naming a nonexistent layer: VERIFY empty result + warning vs silent empty.
Only 2D: entities' Z coordinates ignored/flattened. VERIFY.
$fn at the call affects arc/circle fragment counts — same fragment formula as circle(). VERIFY radius fed per-arc.
DXF versions: old-style (R12-era) entity coding is the well-supported path; newer DXF features simply fall in the unsupported bucket.

dxf_dim(file, name, layer, origin, scale) and dxf_cross(file, layer, origin, scale) remain LIVE functions in 2021.01 reading DIMENSION entities / crossing lines from the same files — decide support or stub-with-warning, but parse them.
impl_notes: Build a DXF probe deck (lines-only loop, lwpolyline closed flag, bulges, arcs, circle, spline, two layers, micro-gaps) and diff the resulting .csg polygons against the oracle. The endpoint-matching tolerance and per-entity warning texts are the compatibility surface.

name: import: SVG
summary: 2D import (2019.05+) of SVG paths and basic shapes into polygons; fill-rule honored, <text> ignored, px units scaled by dpi.

params.name: dpi
params.desc: Conversion for px-denominated lengths: 1px = 25.4/dpi mm. Default 96.

semantics: Supported elements: <path> (full command set including cubic/quadratic beziers and arcs, flattened to segments), <rect> (including rounded corners), <circle>, <ellipse>, <line>, <polyline>, <polygon>, with <g> group transforms applied. fill-rule (nonzero vs evenodd) is respected when resolving self-intersections and holes. Strokes are NOT expanded (stroke properties ignored); only fill geometry imports. Physical units (mm, cm, in, pt, pc) convert exactly; px converts via dpi. The Y axis is flipped so the drawing appears with the same visual orientation as in an SVG viewer.
edge_cases: <text> elements are ignored — VERIFY whether silently or with a warning; convert text to paths before exporting from the drawing tool (documented guidance).

VERIFY placement convention in 2021.01: where the SVG document/viewBox origin lands in OpenSCAD coordinates after the Y flip (top-left at origin with content in y<0, vs content shifted into y>0) — pin via oracle with a known rect; snapshots later added center= which implies the 2021.01 default is NOT centered.
viewBox + width/height scaling honored; VERIFY behavior when width/height are missing (viewBox-only) or when only px sizes given.
CSS support is minimal: presentation attributes and inline style fill/fill-rule/display honored; VERIFY <style> blocks and classes (expected: limited/none in 2021.01).
display:none / visibility: VERIFY respected.
<use>, <defs>, clipPath, mask, gradients: VERIFY — expected unsupported/ignored (fills treated as filled regardless of paint).
Curve flattening consumes $fn/$fa/$fs at the call site. VERIFY the radius/parameter fed to the fragment formula for beziers vs arcs.
Zero-area subpaths and unclosed subpaths: VERIFY (SVG fill semantics implicitly close subpaths — expected: implicit closing).
dpi affects ONLY px-unit lengths; a file authored in mm ignores dpi entirely.
Snapshot-only: id=/layer= selection of specific elements; absent in 2021.01.
impl_notes: The placement/Y-flip convention is the most-reported user surprise — pin it first with a 10x10 rect at viewBox origin. Then fill-rule tests (self-intersecting star nonzero vs evenodd). SVG parsing scope should be documented as exactly this subset; do not silently support more (differential tests would diverge).

name: export: 3D mesh formats (STL, OFF, AMF, 3MF)
summary: 2021.01 3D export surface: binary STL (default for .stl), ASCII STL, OFF, AMF, 3MF — geometry only, no color/units/names beyond fixed boilerplate.
semantics: Export always operates on fully rendered (F6-equivalent) geometry; the GUI forces a render first, the CLI renders implicitly for mesh outputs ($preview=false). Format selected by output extension, overridable/disambiguated with --export-format (needed for ASCII STL since .stl defaults to binary, and for stdout output '-o -').
edge_cases: ASCII STL: header 'solid OpenSCAD_Model' / trailer 'endsolid OpenSCAD_Model'; VERIFY per-facet normal values (computed vs zeros) and the exact float formatting of vertex coordinates in 2021.01 (a reproducible-output change landed around then) — golden STL diffs depend on it.
Binary STL: 80-byte header (VERIFY content), uint32 count, zero attribute bytes.
Exporting when the top-level result is 2D: ERROR approximately 'Current top level object is not a 3D object'. VERIFY text.
Exporting empty geometry: VERIFY — error ('Current top level object is empty') vs empty file; pin.
% background subtrees are excluded from all exports; # debug subtrees are INCLUDED.
color() information is dropped by all four formats in 2021.01 (colored 3MF is Manifold-snapshot-only).
3MF: single object named/structured per lib3mf defaults; units mm. VERIFY object naming/metadata boilerplate if promising byte-level compatibility (recommend not to).
AMF export exists but was already de-emphasized; VERIFY it remains available in 2021.01 GUI menu vs CLI-only.
Vertex/triangle ORDERING in exports is not stable across OpenSCAD versions — promise mesh-level equivalence, not byte-identical files.
Snapshot-only additions: OBJ, WRL, POV exports; colored 3MF.
impl_notes: Decide and document a normalization story: your own exports should be deterministic run-to-run; compare against OpenSCAD via mesh hashing (canonicalized vertex welding), not file bytes. Only ASCII STL text formatting is worth pinning byte-for-byte if your tests parse it.

name: export: 2D formats (DXF, SVG, PDF)
summary: 2D geometry export surface of 2021.01: DXF (pre-2015.03) and SVG (2015.03+), plus PDF (new in 2021.01). Requires the top-level result to be 2D.
semantics: The rendered 2D polygon set (outer boundaries plus holes) is written in millimeter units. DXF writes polyline entities; SVG writes a single document with path data (holes via fill-rule); PDF writes a one-page vector document.
edge_cases: Exporting a 3D result to a 2D format: ERROR approximately 'Current top level object is not a 2D object'. VERIFY text.
DXF export entity choice (LWPOLYLINE vs POLYLINE vs LINE segments): VERIFY and pin — downstream CAM tools are sensitive.

SVG export styling: VERIFY exact fill/stroke attributes (2019.05-era output uses a filled path with stroke; users postprocess it) and the viewBox placement/Y-axis convention (mirrors the import flip).

PDF (2021.01): mm-based, single page; VERIFY page-size selection rule in 2021.01 (fit-to-geometry vs fixed A4/Letter) — snapshot PDFs later grew explicit paper-size options, implying 2021.01 had a fixed simple rule.
All curves are already tessellated — 2D exports contain line segments only, never true arcs/beziers.
% subtrees excluded; # included — same as 3D.
Coordinates: full precision vs %g? VERIFY float formatting per format.
Empty 2D result: VERIFY error vs empty document.
Upstream's 2019.05 release note 'New export file formats: SVG, 3MF, AMF' is sloppy — SVG export shipped in 2015.03; what 2019.05 added on the SVG side was IMPORT.
example:
// shell: openscad -o plate.svg plate.scad
projection(cut = true) translate([0, 0, -1]) cube(10, center = true);
impl_notes: Pin DXF entity types and SVG attribute boilerplate with tiny fixtures (one square with one hole). PDF is a from-scratch writer in a zero-dependency build — keep it minimal (one content stream, no compression is legal PDF) and only match OpenSCAD geometrically.

name: export: PNG image
summary: Renders the scene to a PNG using either the preview pipeline (default; $preview=true) or full render (--render; $preview=false).

params.name: --imgsize
params.desc: Output resolution W,H; default 512,512.

params.name: --camera
params.desc: Either tx,ty,tz,rx,ry,rz,dist (maps to $vpt/$vpr/$vpd) or eyex,eyey,eyez,cx,cy,cz gimbal-free form.

params.name: --colorscheme
params.desc: Named GUI color scheme (e.g. Cornfield default, Tomorrow, DeepOcean...).

params.name: --projection
params.desc: o(rtho) or p(erspective).

semantics: PNG export is the one CLI path where preview semantics apply by default: $preview=true, % background geometry visible (translucent gray), # highlights pink, color() visible. With --render, geometry is fully evaluated and $preview=false. --autocenter and --viewall adjust the camera to the model bounds.
edge_cases: Default camera when --camera absent: the $vp* defaults ([55,0,25], [0,0,0], 140, 22.5) as possibly modified by top-level $vp* assignments in the script.
$preview: plain PNG export -> true; --render -> false; VERIFY --preview=throwntogether also true with the throwntogether renderer.
Pixel-exact PNG comparison against OpenSCAD is NOT a sane compatibility target (GPU/AA variance); OpenSCAD's own test suite uses fuzzy image diffing.
Color scheme names are app surface; unknown name: VERIFY warning + default fallback.
2D geometry PNG export: renders the thin-slab preview look. VERIFY.
VERIFY: -o out.png combined with --export-format png for stdout.
example:
// shell: openscad -o shot.png --imgsize=800,600 --camera=0,0,0,55,0,25,140 model.scad
color("tomato") cube(10, center = true);
impl_notes: Treat PNG as app-level, not language-level, compatibility: match the observable $preview/%/#/color semantics, not pixels. Implement fuzzy-diff harness if you want image regression tests.

name: export: debug/text formats (CSG, AST, TERM, ECHO, NEF3, NEFDBG)
summary: Text-form exports of the evaluation pipeline. The .csg flattened tree is the single most useful differential-testing oracle format; .echo captures console text; .ast dumps the parse; nef3/nefdbg are CGAL internals.
semantics: .csg: the fully evaluated instantiation tree with every variable, loop, function call, and module resolved into a canonical nesting of built-in primitives (group(){...}, cube(size=[...],center=...), multmatrix([[...]]){...}, circle($fn=...,r=...), etc.) — no geometry kernel is run, so it is fast and deterministic. .ast: re-serialization of the parsed source. .term: the CSG term expression dump. .echo: the console message stream (ECHO lines and messages) written to a file. .nef3/.nefdbg: CGAL Nef polyhedron dumps (no reason to reimplement beyond accepting/refusing the extension).
edge_cases: .csg number formatting: VERIFY precision (it is NOT the 6-digit %g of echo; .csg historically prints more digits) — pin exactly, since .csg diffing is your oracle channel.
.csg represents modifiers: VERIFY how *,!,#,% appear (dropped subtrees for *, marker wrappers for #/%).
.csg is itself valid OpenSCAD input (re-importable via rename to .scad) — a strong self-consistency test.
.echo content: VERIFY whether WARNING/ERROR lines are included or only ECHO lines; pin, since CI parses it.
.ast normalizes whitespace/comments away — comments (and thus Customizer annotations) do NOT survive; VERIFY.
nef3/nefdbg: recommend rejecting with a clear 'unsupported in this implementation' error rather than emulating CGAL dumps; they are kernel-internal.
All of these run with $preview=false. VERIFY for .csg (no geometry evaluation happens, but the binding is still set — pin by echoing $preview during a .csg export).
STEP/IGES/BREP are NOT supported in any OpenSCAD version, import or export — do not promise them.
example:
// shell: openscad -o model.csg model.scad
for (i = [0:2]) translate([i * 10, 0, 0]) cube(5);
impl_notes: Implement .csg and .echo first — they are your differential-test backbone against the 2021.01 AppImage. Match the .csg canonical parameter spellings and float format verbatim (probe with every primitive). .ast/.term optional; nef* stubs.

name: Customizer parameter model
signature: top-level 'name = <literal>;' in the MAIN file [+ trailing widget comment]
summary: Which assignments become Customizer parameters: top-level, main-file-only assignments whose right-hand side is a literal (number, string, boolean, or vector of numbers); applied values behave as trailing top-level assignments.
semantics: The Customizer scans the main file's source (comments included) for top-level assignments with literal RHS. Any computed expression (arithmetic, function call, reference to another variable) disqualifies the variable — it evaluates normally but shows no widget. Documented guidance: parameters must appear before the first module/function definition to be recognized (the scanner stops there). include'd files' variables are never shown. When the user changes a value (or a preset/-D applies one), the effect is 'as if assigned at the end of the top-level scope' — winning under last-write-wins; the script cannot distinguish customized values from its own literals.
edge_cases: VERIFY the exact cutoff rule: 'parameters before the first module/function definition' is the documented guidance; pin whether assignments after the first definition are truly ignored or still picked up in 2021.01.
VERIFY: negative number literals (a = -5;) count as literals and get widgets.
Vector parameters: vector of NUMBER literals only, and the panel renders up to 4 components; VERIFY behavior for length > 4 (not shown vs first 4).
a = true; -> checkbox; a = "text"; -> text box; a = 5; -> spinbox (no comment) — the widget kinds are fixed by RHS type plus comment.
An assignment reassigned later in the file: VERIFY which occurrence the panel binds to (last-write-wins evaluation vs first-scan) — pin; users hit this with 'derived = param;' patterns.
undef literal RHS: VERIFY (expected: not customizable).
Nothing in the language exposes 'was customized'; version()/feature probes cannot detect it either — by design.
The GUI hides the panel entirely for files with no recognizable parameters.
Parameters inside 'if' blocks or modules are never customizable (not top-level).
Comment scanning requires the implementation's lexer to RETAIN or re-scan comments — a comment-discarding lexer cannot implement the Customizer.
impl_notes: Implement as a separate comment-aware scan over the main file's token stream, independent of evaluation. This is the machine interface for your MCP parameter discovery — make the scan's output a stable JSON schema (name, type, widget, group, description, default) and oracle-pin the cutoff/duplicate rules.

name: Customizer widget comment grammar
signature: value; // [min:max] | [min:step:max] | [max] | [v1, v2, ...] | [v1:label1, v2:label2, ...] | <N>   (+ '// description' on the line above)
summary: The trailing-comment mini-language that selects the widget for a parameter, and the preceding-line description comment.

params.name: [min:max]
params.desc: Slider from min to max. VERIFY step inference: 1 for integer bounds; pin decimal-bounds behavior.

params.name: [min:step:max]
params.desc: Slider with explicit step.

params.name: [max]
params.desc: Slider from 0 to max.

params.name: [a, b, c]
params.desc: Combo box (dropdown) of allowed values; numbers or unquoted strings.

params.name: [val:Label, ...]
params.desc: Combo box with display labels; stored value is the part before ':'.

params.name: <N> (bare number comment, strings)
params.desc: VERIFY: for string parameters, '// 12' sets the text box maximum input length.

params.name: // description (line above)
params.desc: A '//' comment on the line immediately above the assignment becomes the parameter's tooltip/description text.

semantics: The comment must trail the assignment on the same line (after the ';'). Widget by type+comment: number+range -> slider; number no comment -> spinbox; number+list -> dropdown; string+list -> dropdown; string no comment -> textbox; boolean -> checkbox (comment ignored); vector (<=4 numeric elements) -> one spinner/slider per component, with a single range comment applying to every component.
edge_cases: Labeled values: '// [10:Small, 20:Large]' — labels may contain spaces; VERIFY whether labels may contain ':' or ',' (expected: no escaping mechanism).
String dropdowns use UNQUOTED values in the comment ('// [red, green, blue]'); the assignment RHS is a quoted string and must match one entry to preselect.
VERIFY: '// [max]' single-value slider form (0..max) exists in OpenSCAD proper (Thingiverse-inherited grammar) — pin.
Malformed range comments (e.g. '// [a:b]' with non-numbers on a number param): VERIFY fallback (expected: treated as plain spinbox / dropdown attempt; no console warning).
Whitespace tolerance inside brackets: '// [ 0 : 5 ]' — VERIFY accepted.
A range comment on a boolean or a list comment on a bool: comment ignored, checkbox stands. VERIFY.
Vector + range: '// [0:50]' bounds every component; per-component ranges do not exist.
Description comment must be IMMEDIATELY above (no blank line); VERIFY blank-line tolerance and multi-line ('//' stacked) behavior.
VERIFY: step in '[min:step:max]' with step > span, zero step, min > max — pin GUI behavior (expected: unusable/clamped silently; no console warnings — the Customizer never warns).
The grammar lives in comments: /* */ block comments trailing the line are NOT widget comments (only '//'). VERIFY.
Unicode in labels/descriptions passes through (UTF-8).
example:
// Wall thickness of the box
wall = 2; // [0.5:0.1:5]
finish = "matte"; // [matte:Matte, gloss:High gloss]
size = [20, 30]; // [10:100]
impl_notes: Write the comment grammar as a real grammar with tests, not regex soup — Thingiverse/Printables models exercise every corner. All VERIFY items are cheap GUI-observation probes against 2021.01; none affect evaluation, only the panel and your MCP schema.

name: Customizer group tabs: /* [Group] */, [Hidden], [Global]
summary: Block comments containing a bracketed name partition subsequent parameters into named tabs; [Hidden] suppresses parameters from the panel; [Global] parameters appear in every tab.
semantics: A block comment whose entire content is '[Name]' starts a section: all following parameters (until the next section comment) belong to that tab. The special name 'Hidden' removes subsequent parameters from the panel entirely (they remain ordinary variables, still overridable via -D and presets — VERIFY preset applicability). The special name 'Global' makes its parameters visible in every tab. Parameters before any section comment go in an unnamed default section.
edge_cases: 'Hidden' and 'Global' are case-sensitive magic names. VERIFY case sensitivity.
VERIFY: whether presets/-P apply values to Hidden parameters (expected: yes for -D; pin for preset sets saved by the GUI, which only round-trips visible widgets).
Reusing the same group name later in the file: VERIFY merge into one tab vs duplicate tab.
Tab order = order of first appearance in the source.
The section comment must be a standalone block comment '/* [Name] */'; VERIFY tolerance for extra whitespace and for '//'-style section comments (expected: block comments only).
Groups have no nesting.
A group with zero recognizable parameters: VERIFY whether an empty tab shows (expected: no).
Hidden is commonly used to keep derived-constant assignments from cluttering the panel even though computed RHS already disqualifies them — harmless overlap.
impl_notes: Straightforward once the comment-aware scanner exists. Expose group membership in your MCP parameter schema; pin the two magic names' exact matching rules by GUI observation.

name: Customizer preset JSON
summary: Preset parameter sets saved beside the model as JSON; applied in the GUI or via CLI -p file.json -P setName.

params.name: fileFormatVersion
params.desc: String "1" in 2021.01.

params.name: parameterSets
params.desc: Object mapping set names to objects mapping parameter names to VALUES ENCODED AS STRINGS (numbers as "5", vectors as "[1, 2]", booleans as "true").

semantics: The GUI's +/- preset controls read and write this file (default name: same basename as the .scad file with .json). Applying a set assigns each named parameter as-if at the end of the top-level scope (same mechanism as the panel). CLI: 'openscad -p sets.json -P setName -o out.stl model.scad' applies the set headlessly.
edge_cases: Values are JSON STRINGS containing OpenSCAD literal syntax, not native JSON numbers/arrays — VERIFY whether 2021.01 also tolerates native JSON types on read (be liberal only if the oracle is).
Vector values as strings include brackets and comma-space: "[1, 2, 3]" — VERIFY exact serialization the GUI writes (your writer should match for round-trip).
-P naming a set absent from the file: VERIFY warning text and whether export proceeds with defaults.
A set entry naming a parameter that does not exist in the model: VERIFY ignored silently vs warned.
A set value for a computed (non-customizable) variable: VERIFY — since application is 'trailing assignment', it may still override; pin.
GUI maintains a 'design default values' entry semantics for unsaved state — VERIFY whether that name appears in the JSON or is app-only.
String parameter values are stored as the raw string WITHOUT extra quotes inside the JSON string. VERIFY.
-p without -P: VERIFY behavior (expected: no set applied).
Malformed JSON file: VERIFY error text.
$-variables in presets: VERIFY whether the GUI ever writes them and whether -P applies them.
impl_notes: This file IS your MCP preset interface — implement reader and writer, round-trip-stable, matching the GUI's string-encoded serialization byte-for-byte where feasible. Every VERIFY here is a five-minute CLI probe.

name: -D name=value injection (CLI overrides)
summary: Ad-hoc command-line overrides injected as trailing top-level assignments in the main file's scope — they win under last-write-wins over everything textual.

params.name: name
params.desc: Any variable name, including $-specials ($fn, $t, $preview...).

params.name: expr
params.desc: A full OpenSCAD expression, not just a literal; strings need embedded quotes: -D 'label="hi"'.

semantics: Each -D appends an assignment after the main file's own top-level statements, in command-line order. Because assignment is last-write-wins taking effect at the name's first-assignment slot, a -D value effectively replaces the in-file value everywhere. Reaches: main-file variables and (since include'd assignments share the main scope) included-file variables. Cannot reach: use'd files' private variables, or any non-top-level binding.
edge_cases: Multiple -D for the SAME name: later command-line occurrence wins (it is the later 'write').
VERIFY: interaction order with -p/-P presets — expected: preset applied first, -D applied after, so -D beats the preset; pin.

expr is evaluated as an expression in the top scope: it may reference other top-level variables ('-D h=w*2'). VERIFY evaluation-order edge when it references a variable defined textually later (first-assignment-slot semantics make this subtle — pin).
Invalid expression syntax in -D: VERIFY error text and whether the run aborts.
-D 'x=' (empty): VERIFY.

Overriding a variable the file never defines: creates a new top-level variable (harmless; readable by the script if it references it — but a bare reference to it in the file would have warned before injection? No: injection happens before evaluation, so the name exists. VERIFY warning behavior).
-D can set $fn/$t/$preview/$vp* — standard automation idioms; must hit the same last-write-wins override path.
Shell quoting eats a layer: the canonical string form is -D 'name="value"'; document it.
-D applies only to the main file — a variable name that exists only in a use'd file is NOT affected (a new same-named main-scope variable appears instead, unused).
impl_notes: Implement literally as appended assignments to the parsed main file before evaluation — that single mechanism reproduces every precedence quirk automatically. Pin the -D-vs-preset ordering and the forward-reference case with oracle probes.

name: number formatting (6 significant digits)
signature: format(x) — double-conversion library, 6 significant digits — shared by echo, str(), assert messages, and value-embedding warnings
summary: All user-visible number-to-text conversion in 2021.01 uses %g with 6 significant digits: trailing zeros trimmed, no decimal point for integer values, scientific notation for large/small magnitudes — famously rounding large integers.
semantics: Rules (2021.01, double-conversion library at 6 significant digits): fixed notation for 1e-5 <= |x| < 1e6, scientific otherwise; lowercase 'e' with explicit sign and NO zero padding of the exponent; at most 6 significant digits; trailing zeros trimmed and a bare decimal point stripped; -0 prints as 0 (UNIQUE_ZERO). Examples: 1/3 -> 0.333333; PI -> 3.14159; 10.0 -> 10; 100000 -> 100000; 1000000 -> 1e+6; 1234567 -> 1.23457e+6; 0.0001 -> 0.0001; 0.00001 -> 0.00001; 1.1e-6 -> 1.1e-6; 1e100 -> 1e+100; 0.1+0.2 -> 0.3 (error hidden by rounding). inf -> inf, -inf -> -inf, nan -> nan. Pre-2021 releases used printf %g (zero-padded exponents like 1e+06 and scientific already at 1e-5, printing 1e-05) — 2021.01 is exactly where the formatter changed.
edge_cases: Large-integer trap: any |x| >= 1e6 goes scientific AND gets rounded to 6 digits — echo(1234567) prints 1.23457e+6; str() inherits this, so user string-building silently corrupts big numbers. Must clone.
Exponent format: lowercase 'e', explicit sign, NO zero padding — '1e+6', '1.1e-6', '1e+100'. (Pre-2021 %g output padded to two digits: '1e+06'.)
-0 prints as '0' (UNIQUE_ZERO flag in the 2021.01 formatter); the sign survives arithmetic — 1/-0 == -inf.
0.5 -> 0.5; the small-number scientific switch is BELOW 1e-5: 0.0001 and 0.00001 both print fixed ('0.0001', '0.00001'); 1.1e-6 prints '1.1e-6'.

Rounding is round-half-even per printf? VERIFY the tie behavior at the 6th digit (printf uses the current FP rounding, effectively round-half-even on the decimal conversion) — matters only for exact-tie goldens.
true/false/undef are NOT numbers; booleans print true/false.
The same formatter renders numbers INSIDE vectors and named-argument values.
.csg export and STL/AMF writers use DIFFERENT (higher) precision — do not unify the formatters. VERIFY each writer's precision separately.
Dev snapshots have moved toward shortest-round-trip full precision output — 2021.01 baseline stays 6-digit double-conversion output; only chase snapshot behavior behind an explicit flag.
str(1/3) == "0.333333" exactly — string-comparison user code depends on it.
since: precision (6 sig digits) pre-2015.03; formatter changed to double-conversion in 2021.01 (unpadded exponents, -0 prints 0)
impl_notes: Implement one canonical dtoa-%g(6) routine, byte-identical to glibc printf %g for the reachable domain, and use it for echo/str/assert/warnings ONLY. Golden-test a sweep: powers of ten 1e-7..1e7, ties, negatives, -0, inf, nan, and the 999999.5 boundary.

name: value display forms (echo/str rendering of every type)
signature: display(v): number -> %g6 | string -> "quoted" (echo) / bare (str) | vector -> [a, b, c] | range -> [b : s : e] | bool -> true/false | undef -> undef | function -> source-like
summary: The per-type textual rendering shared by echo, assert messages, and (with the string-quoting exception) str().
semantics: Vectors: '[' + elements joined by ', ' + ']', recursive, with strings quoted inside regardless of echo/str context. Ranges: bracketed with SPACED colons, e.g. [0 : 1 : 10]. Booleans: true/false. undef: undef. Function values (2021.01): a source-like rendering of the literal. Strings: quoted with '"' by echo and inside containers; emitted bare by str() at top level. Numbers: the shared %g6 formatter.
edge_cases: VERIFY: range display always shows three fields including an implicit step 1 ([0 : 1 : 10] for [0:10]) — pin; also whether the ORIGINAL begin/end are shown for the deprecated reversed range or the swapped ones.
str([1, "a"]) -> '[1, "a"]' — strings inside vectors ARE quoted even via str(); only a top-level string argument is bare. Must clone this asymmetry.
Interior quotes/backslashes in strings are NOT escaped on output (echo("a\"b") -> "a"b") — output is not re-parseable; VERIFY exact bytes.
Nested vectors: '[[1, 2], [3, 4]]' — comma-space everywhere, no line breaks, no length limits (a huge vector prints huge; GUI may truncate display — app behavior; VERIFY CLI never truncates).

Function literal rendering: approximately 'function(x, y = 1) body-expression-ish' — VERIFY exact text (whether the body prints or elides) via oracle; it appears in echo output of BOSL2-style debugging.
Empty vector: '[]'; empty string via echo: '""'; via str(): ''.
Named-arg wrapper: 'name = ' + display(value).
Ranges never expand to elements in display (they are a distinct type).
VERIFY: -0, inf, nan inside vectors use the same tokens (e.g. [inf, nan]).
example:
echo([1, "a", true, undef], [0:10], str("x=", [1, "a"]));
// ECHO: [1, "a", true, undef], [0 : 1 : 10], "x=[1, \"a\"]"  <- VERIFY: quotes NOT escaped in real output
impl_notes: One recursive display function with an 'outermost string bare?' flag covers echo vs str. Pin range and function-literal renderings via oracle first — they are the two genuinely uncertain spots.

name: diagnostic message surface (WARNING / ERROR / DEPRECATED / TRACE)
signature: "WARNING: <msg>[, in file <path>, line <N>]" | "ERROR: ..." | "DEPRECATED: ..." | "TRACE: called by '<module>', in file <path>, line <N>"
summary: The console diagnostic grammar: prefixes, file/line suffixes, TRACE unwinding, emission order, and the --hardwarnings contract. Users and CI parse these strings; the emitted SET of warnings is itself compatibility surface.
semantics: Messages are emitted in depth-first instantiation/evaluation order, interleaved with ECHO lines, before/independent of geometry rendering. Warnings never halt evaluation (undef propagates instead); ERRORs from assert/fatal conditions halt; DEPRECATED marks legacy constructs; TRACE lines follow an ERROR to unwind the module stack. --hardwarnings promotes any WARNING to a fatal error (serious users run CI with it, so both the texts AND the set of conditions that warn must match).
edge_cases: Known 2021.01 warning conditions to reproduce (texts approximate — VERIFY each verbatim against the binary): variable reassignment ('WARNING: variable a was reassigned...'); unknown variable ('Ignoring unknown variable ...'); unknown module ('Ignoring unknown module ...'); unknown function ('Ignoring unknown function ...'); unknown named parameter; unequal-length or scalar-vector +/- ('undefined operation ...'); division by zero; $fa/$fs clamped to 0.01; deprecated reversed range; deprecated assign(); deprecated triangles=; empty min()/max(); out-of-domain math (2019.05+); range step 0; too many unused parameters — plus the per-format import warnings.

VERIFY the file/line suffix pattern per message class: some messages embed ', in file <path>, line <N>' (comma-separated, period-terminated), some historically omitted location — pin each probe case; your MCP layer will regex them.
DEPRECATED examples: 'DEPRECATED: The assign() module will be removed in future releases. Use a regular assignment instead.' and the [begin:end] reversed-range message. VERIFY texts.
TRACE format: one line per module frame, innermost first, quoting the module name in single quotes. VERIFY whether anonymous frames (for/if groups) appear.
Emission count: a warning inside a loop fires per iteration; the GUI console may rate-limit repeated identical lines (app behavior, not language — the CLI stream does not).
is_undef(x) on an unknown name suppresses the unknown-variable warning (documented guard); bare reference warns.
--hardwarnings stops at the FIRST warning; exit code nonzero. VERIFY exit codes for warning-stop vs error-stop.
Message stream destination on CLI is stderr; -o out.echo captures (VERIFY whether warnings are included in .echo).
Warnings emitted during expression evaluation (e.g. inside a function) appear at the position of the triggering top-level instantiation in stream order — pin ordering with an interleaved probe.
example:
a = 1; a = 2;        // WARNING: variable a was reassigned ...
b = [1, 2] + 1;      // WARNING (no broadcasting) and b == undef
echo(b);             // ECHO: undef
impl_notes: Treat the warning catalog as a frozen enum: one probe .scad per condition, transcript captured from the 2021.01 AppImage, goldens checked verbatim in CI. Build --hardwarnings from day one (first-warning abort) — retrofitting halting semantics into a warn-and-continue evaluator is invasive.

name: Variables & scoping
summary: OpenSCAD assignment is declarative, not imperative: within one scope the textually LAST assignment to a name provides its single value, effective at the position of the FIRST assignment; every { } block is a child scope that can only shadow, never mutate, outer bindings; variables, functions, and modules live in three separate namespaces with hoisted definitions; there is no mutation anywhere in the language.

params.name: name = expr;
params.desc: Assignment statement. The first textual assignment to a name in a scope creates that name's slot at that position; later assignments in the SAME scope replace the expression stored in that original slot (last-write-wins) and emit a reassignment warning. No compound assignment (+=, ++, --) exists.

params.name: { } block scopes
params.desc: Module bodies, if/else branches, for bodies, let bodies, and bare { } grouping blocks are each a child scope. Assignments inside always create fresh shadowing bindings; they can never modify an enclosing scope's variable.

params.name: module/function definitions
params.desc: Lexically scoped and hoisted within their scope: callable before their textual definition. Duplicate definitions in one scope warn, last wins. They occupy namespaces separate from variables — one identifier can simultaneously name a variable, a function, and a module; syntax disambiguates (statement call = module, expression call = function, bare name = variable).

params.name: let (a=e1, b=e2) ...
params.desc: Expression form and (2019.05+) statement form. Bindings evaluate SEQUENTIALLY, each seeing earlier ones; creates a new scope shadowing outer names; there is no last-write-wins across let bindings.

params.name: assign (a=1) { ... }
params.desc: Deprecated ancestor of the let statement; still parses and works in 2021.01 with a deprecation warning. Legacy scripts use it — must be supported.

params.name: include <f> / use <f>
params.desc: include splices the file's top level into the including scope (its assignments join the same last-write-wins arena, with the main file's assignment overriding the included file's); use imports only module/function definitions, evaluating the used file's top-level variables privately (2019.05+).

params.name: -D name=value / customizer presets
params.desc: Injected as assignments appended at the END of the top-level scope, so they beat in-file assignments via last-write-wins. The script cannot distinguish overridden values from literals.

semantics: Each lexical scope holds an ordered list of assignment slots plus a list of other statements (module instantiations, echo, assert, if/for, etc.). The first textual assignment to a name creates that name's slot at that position; any later assignment to the same name in the same scope replaces the expression in the ORIGINAL slot rather than creating a new binding, and emits a reassignment warning. When the scope is instantiated, assignment slots are evaluated in slot order, and the scope's non-assignment statements then execute against the final values — so 'a=1; echo(a); a=5;' prints ECHO: 5, and 'a=1; b=a; a=2;' yields b==2 (a's slot, holding the winning expression 2, evaluates before b's slot). Forward references between assignments do NOT work: an assignment whose RHS names a variable whose only slot comes later in the same scope (and which is not bound in an enclosing scope) reads undef with an unknown-variable warning — variables are not hoisted the way definitions are. Child scopes see enclosing bindings lexically; an inner assignment shadows for that scope only, which is why 'x=5; if (c) { x=6; }' leaves outer x at 5 and conditional values must be written 'x = c ? a : b;'. There is no while, break, continue, return, or any mutation; all iteration is data-driven and all function logic is a single expression. Module parameters bind positionally then by name (named args in any order); a missing parameter without a default is undef; defaults may reference EARLIER parameters of the same signature. This model is a compatibility contract: an implementation that 'fixes' last-write-wins or block shadowing to be imperative breaks real scripts, and the documented library-override idiom (assign in the including file to override an include'd library default) depends on it.
edge_cases: a=1; b=a; a=2; yields b==2: the winning expression evaluates at a's original (first) slot position, before b's slot. A warning is emitted. VERIFY: exact 2021.01 reassignment warning text — believed of the form 'WARNING: a was assigned on line 1 but was overwritten' plus file/line; capture verbatim from the oracle.
a=1; echo(a); a=5; prints ECHO: 5 — non-assignment statements in a scope observe the scope's FINAL variable values, even when textually between the two assignments.

VERIFY: exact interleaving of assignment evaluation vs statement execution (believed: all of a scope's assignments evaluate, in slot order, before any of its instantiations run) — pin with echo probes mixing assignments and echoes.

Forward reference among assignments fails: 'b=a; a=2;' gives b=undef with an unknown-variable warning (approx 'WARNING: Ignoring unknown variable 'a''). VERIFY the warning fires here and the exact text.

Self-reference: in a child scope with an outer x, 'x = x + 1;' reads the OUTER x (outer x=5 gives inner x==6) because the RHS is evaluated before the inner binding exists. VERIFY: at top level 'x=1; x=x+1;' collapses both assignments into one slot whose winning expression references its own name — believed to produce undef plus unknown-variable and reassignment warnings, NOT 2. Pin both cases.

VERIFY: 'x=5; if (true) { echo(x); x=6; }' — believed the inner echo prints 6 (the inner scope has its own hoisted-slot x whose assignments complete before inner statements run), while echo after the block prints 5.
VERIFY: whether 2021.01 emits any warning when a child-scope assignment shadows an outer variable (some historical versions warned; believed silent in 2021.01).

Reading a never-assigned variable warns approx 'WARNING: Ignoring unknown variable 'foo'' and yields undef; is_undef(foo) performs the same probe WITHOUT the warning — the idiomatic defined-guard. This asymmetry is load-bearing for libraries.
Three namespaces: 'r=5; function r(x)=x*2; module r(){ sphere(r); } r(); echo(r(3), r);' is legal — all three coexist and are resolved by syntactic position.

Hoisting: modules and functions are callable before their textual definition within the same scope; mutual recursion between two definitions in one scope works regardless of order. Variables get no such treatment.
Duplicate module or function definition in one scope: WARNING, last definition wins. VERIFY exact warning text.

VERIFY: user redefinition of a builtin (e.g. 'module cube() { sphere(1); }') — believed user definitions shadow builtins for calls resolved in their scope; pin precedence and whether any warning is emitted.

let bindings are sequential ('let(a=1, b=a+1)' gives b==2) and do NOT use last-write-wins. VERIFY: duplicate name within one let ('let(a=1, a=a+1) a') — believed the later binding shadows the earlier sequentially yielding 2, possibly with a warning.
assign(a=1) { ... } still works in 2021.01 with a deprecation message. VERIFY exact text, approx 'DEPRECATED: assign is deprecated. Use a regular assignment instead.'

Module/function calls: positional args first, then named args in any order; missing param without default = undef; defaults may reference earlier parameters ('module m(a, b=a)'); an unknown NAMED argument produces a WARNING and is ignored (VERIFY text, approx 'WARNING: variable p not specified as parameter') — EXCEPT $-prefixed arguments, which are always accepted silently (see the $-environment chapter).
include has no include-guards: double inclusion re-executes top-level geometry, re-defines modules/functions (duplicate-definition warnings), and re-runs assignments.

include override rule: an assignment in the INCLUDING (main) file overrides the included file's assignment of the same name regardless of textual order — this is the documented library-customization pattern. VERIFY specifically the case where the override assignment textually PRECEDES the include directive.

use <f> is top-level only (error inside blocks); the used file's top-level variables are evaluated in its own private scope so its functions/modules can see them (2019.05+), but they are invisible to and not overridable by the user. VERIFY pre-2019.05 difference (used files' top-level variables previously not evaluated).

-D name=value CLI defines and customizer preset application behave as trailing top-level assignments and therefore win via last-write-wins; the customizer panel itself only recognizes top-level LITERAL assignments in the main file.
The for loop variable is bound immutably per iteration in a child scope; assigning to it inside the body creates a shadow and does not affect iteration.
Each module instantiation re-evaluates the body's assignments from scratch — no state persists between calls.
Bare { } blocks are legal statements (grouping) and are scopes: assignments inside do not leak.
Geometry is not a value: 'x = cube(1);' is a syntax/semantic error — statements and expressions are disjoint grammars (see Geometry model chapter).
No semicolon is written after a { } block; assignments require the trailing semicolon.
impl_notes: Implement each scope as an ordered map of slots: parse-time, record first-occurrence position per name and overwrite the stored expression on reassignment (recording the warning); eval-time, evaluate slots in order into an environment frame, then execute statements. Oracle probes to pin before freezing: exact reassignment warning text; forward-reference and self-reference (x=x+1 top-level vs child-scope) results and warning sets; shadow-warning presence; include-override with pre-include assignment; duplicate let bindings; builtin shadowing precedence; unknown-named-argument warning text. The is_undef() warning suppression needs a special evaluation mode for its argument (lookup-without-warning). Keep -D/preset injection literally as appended assignments so last-write-wins does the work.

name: The $-environment
signature:
$fa = 6; $fs = 0.5;                 // file scope: defaults for the whole tree
module tower() { $fn = 4; children(); }  // children get $fn=4 dynamically
tower() cylinder(h=8, r=3);
sphere(2, $fn=16);                  // per-call override, no declaration needed
ring($steps = 6) circle(1);         // any user-invented $name flows the same way
summary: Every $-prefixed variable — builtin ($fn, $fa, $fs, $t, $vpr, $vpt, $vpd, $vpf, $children, $preview, $parent_modules) or user-invented — is dynamically scoped down the instantiation/call stack: a binding set in any scope, or passed as an undeclared named argument to any call, is visible to all descendant module instantiations and function calls, and children() bodies combine the caller's lexical scope with the callee's $-environment.

params.name: $fn
params.desc: Fragment count override for circle tessellation; default 0 (meaning 'use $fa/$fs formula'). When > 0 the fragment count is max($fn, 3); fractional values truncated (VERIFY truncation vs ceil).

params.name: $fa
params.desc: Minimum angle per fragment, degrees; default 12; clamped to >= 0.01 with a WARNING.

params.name: $fs
params.desc: Minimum arc length per fragment, units; default 2; clamped to >= 0.01 with a WARNING.

params.name: $t
params.desc: Animation time in [0,1); default 0; driven by the GUI animation panel (FPS x Steps) or CLI; models read it like any variable.

params.name: $vpr / $vpt / $vpd / $vpf
params.desc: Viewport rotation [x,y,z] degrees (default [55,0,25]), translation (default [0,0,0]), camera distance (default 140), FOV degrees (default 22.5). Reads return the live GUI camera; top-level assignments set the camera after each preview frame (animatable camera). $vpf is NEW in 2021.01.

params.name: $children
params.desc: Number of children passed to the currently executing module; 0 at top level and in childless calls.

params.name: $preview
params.desc: true during F5/OpenCSG preview and PNG export with --preview; false during F6 render and CLI mesh/2D exports. Added 2019.05.

params.name: $parent_modules
params.desc: Depth of the module instantiation stack; companion to parent_module(n).

params.name: $<user-name>
params.desc: Any user-invented $-name participates in the identical dynamic-scoping machinery with no declaration anywhere; unset reads yield undef.

semantics: The evaluator carries two environments: the lexical scope chain (ordinary names, resolved at definition sites) and the dynamic $-environment (a stack of $-bindings snapshotted along the instantiation/call path). Setting a $-variable with an ordinary assignment in any scope rebinds it for every module instantiation and function call made within that scope's dynamic extent — descendants only, never siblings or ancestors. Additionally, ANY module or function call may include $name=value named arguments that the callee never declared; these are accepted silently (unlike unknown plain named arguments, which warn) and become dynamic bindings for the callee's entire subtree/evaluation. children() is the subtle case: the child statements passed at a call site evaluate lazily when the callee invokes children(), using the CALLER's lexical scope for ordinary names but the CALLEE's current $-environment — so a module that sets $fn=64 before children() re-tessellates the children it was handed. Function literals capture their lexical definition environment as a closure, but $-references inside their bodies still resolve dynamically at each call. The tessellation specials feed one exact formula for the fragment count of a full circle of radius r: if r < GRID_FINE (2^-20, about 9.537e-7) then 3 fragments; else if $fn > 0 then max($fn, 3); else ceil(max(min(360/$fa, 2*PI*r/$fs), 5)) — i.e. $fa caps angle per fragment, $fs caps arc length, whichever demands FEWER fragments wins the min() — both act as caps and the coarser cap governs — with the result then floored at 5. Consumers of this formula: circle, sphere (meridian count; latitude rings = ceil(N/2) at half-step phase), cylinder (using max(r1,r2)), rotate_extrude (scaled by angle/360), offset(r), text() outline flattening, and linear_extrude's default slices under twist. Getting dynamic scoping wrong breaks BOSL2 and most serious libraries.
edge_cases: Every $-prefixed name is dynamically scoped — the machinery is not limited to builtins; user-defined $-flags ($slop, $my_debug) are pervasive in libraries.
Any call site may pass $foo=val without the callee declaring it: no 'unknown parameter' warning is emitted for $-arguments (plain unknown named arguments DO warn and are ignored).
Reading an unset $-variable yields undef. VERIFY: believed NO unknown-variable warning is emitted for $-names (unlike plain variables) — pin, because warning parity matters under --hardwarnings.
Builtin specials have global defaults, so echo($fn) at top level prints 0, not undef; user $-vars have no default and read undef until bound.

children() environment split: 'module m(){ $fn=64; children(); } m() sphere(5);' renders the sphere with $fn=64, while ordinary variables in the child expression (e.g. 'm() sphere(r=q);') resolve in the caller's lexical scope. Child arguments are evaluated lazily at each children() instantiation, not eagerly at the call site.
Each children()/children(i) call re-instantiates under the $-environment in force at THAT call — a callee can stamp the same children twice with different $fn values.
