Function calls (named functions and function literals) receive the caller's current $-environment; closures capture lexical names only — $-names always resolve dynamically at call time.

Fragment formula, exact: r < 2^-20 gives 3 fragments; $fn > 0 gives max($fn, 3) (VERIFY: fractional $fn believed truncated toward zero, not rounded/ceiled); otherwise ceil(max(min(360/$fa, 2*PI*r/$fs), 5)).
$fa and $fs are clamped to a minimum of 0.01 with a WARNING. VERIFY exact text, approx 'WARNING: $fa too small - clamping to 0.01' / 'WARNING: $fs too small - clamping to 0.01'.
VERIFY: negative or zero $fn — believed the '$fn > 0' test fails and the $fa/$fs formula applies (i.e. negative $fn behaves like unset).
$fn between 1 and 3 yields 3 fragments (max($fn,3) floor).
Setting a $-var inside a for body, if branch, or let block scopes the binding to that subtree; each for iteration can carry its own $-bindings.

Top-level assignments to $vpr/$vpt/$vpd/$vpf set the camera AFTER each preview frame (enabling $t-driven camera animation); reads inside the GUI return the live camera the user has navigated to, so a re-preview can observe changed values. VERIFY interaction with CLI --camera (believed CLI camera flags take precedence for image export).

$preview is true for F5 preview and for PNG export with --preview, false for F6 render and all CLI mesh/2D exports. Idioms to support: '$fn = $preview ? 24 : 120;' and skipping minkowski in preview. VERIFY whether -D '$preview=true' can override the pipeline-provided value.
$t defaults to 0 outside animation; the GUI animation panel (FPS x Steps) sweeps it through [0,1); models simply read it. Your app must define how it drives $t.

$children is set by the module-call machinery per invocation (0 at top level); $parent_modules likewise per instantiation stack depth. VERIFY: manually assigning $children or $parent_modules — believed treated as an ordinary dynamic binding that shadows the machinery value for descendants; pin the observable result.
Passing specials to primitives is per-call dynamic binding: sphere(10, $fn=64) affects only that subtree; the file-level $fn is untouched.
A $-argument passed to a module call is part of the callee's $-environment and therefore also reaches the callee's children() instantiations.
VERIFY: $-assignments at the top level of a use'd file — believed private to that file's scope and NOT injected into callers (dynamic bindings flow from the call stack, not from definition sites).
$-variables hold any value type (vectors for $vpr, booleans for user flags); no type checking occurs at binding time — consumers warn/misbehave on bad types when they read them.
Dynamic lookup order: the innermost binding on the current instantiation/call stack wins; there is no way to read 'one level up' past a shadowing binding.
The $-environment never flows upward or sideways: a callee cannot alter its caller's $-values.
impl_notes: Represent the dynamic environment as an immutable stack snapshot captured per instantiation/call; children must be stored as (AST, caller lexical env) closures whose $-env is supplied at children() time. The fragment formula and its consumers must match bit-for-bit — real models depend on exact fragment counts. Oracle probes: unset-$ warning behavior, fractional/negative $fn, clamp warning texts, $preview value under every CLI export mode, camera read/write semantics, manual assignment to $children/$parent_modules. $vpf is 2021.01-only; $preview is 2019.05+ — report undef for them only if you deliberately emulate older baselines.

name: Type system & truthiness
summary: OpenSCAD values are: number (f64), boolean, string, vector, range, and undef — plus first-class function values since 2021.01 (and an experimental object type in snapshots only). Type mismatches never throw: they produce undef plus a console WARNING and evaluation continues. Equality (==/!=) is total deep structural comparison; ordering (< <= > >=) is partial (numbers and strings only, else undef). Truthiness: false, 0, "", [], and undef are falsy (exactly five values); everything else — including "false", [0], -1, and nan — is truthy.

params.name: number
params.desc: IEEE-754 double; the only numeric type. nan and inf are values of it, but is_num(nan) is false.

params.name: boolean
params.desc: true/false literals; never coerces to/from numbers (1 == true is false).

params.name: string
params.desc: Immutable UTF-8 text indexed by Unicode code point; s[i] yields a 1-character string (no char type); not a list (is_list false) but iterable.

params.name: vector
params.desc: The only container: heterogeneous, arbitrarily nested list written [a, b, c]. Also serves as matrix (nested rows) and point.

params.name: range
params.desc: [begin:end] / [begin:step:end]; a distinct lazy type — is_list false, len undef, indexing undef. See the Ranges chapter.

params.name: undef
params.desc: The absent/error value: undefined variables, missing parameters, out-of-range indexing, and every type-mismatched operation produce it (usually with a WARNING).

params.name: function
params.desc: First-class function value from a 'function (x) expr' literal; NEW in 2021.01; tested with is_function.

params.name: object
params.desc: SNAPSHOT-ONLY experimental dict-like type (textmetrics results), with dot access and is_object(); absent from 2021.01.

semantics: The language is dynamically typed with no coercions of any kind: arithmetic on non-numbers, '+' on strings, comparisons across categories, and similar mismatches yield undef accompanied by a console WARNING (approximately 'WARNING: undefined operation ...' naming the operand types — the warning text and count are observable surface), and evaluation always continues; nothing throws except assert(). undef then propagates silently through further operations (each new mismatched operation warns again). Equality == and inequality != are TOTAL: defined for every pair of values, comparing deeply and structurally — vectors elementwise with length equality required, mismatched types simply unequal (false, never undef), undef == undef true, and nan unequal to everything including itself. Relational operators < <= > >= are PARTIAL: defined only for number-number (IEEE semantics) and string-string (lexicographic by Unicode code point); every other combination evaluates to undef. These are two deliberately different comparison regimes in one language and both must be cloned. Truthiness (used by if, the ternary, !, &&, ||, and comprehension filters): exactly false, 0, the empty string "", the empty vector [], and undef are falsy (five values); every other value is truthy — including the strings "false" and "0", the vectors [0], [[]] and [false], negative numbers, inf, and nan (truthiness is a plain != 0 test with no isnan carve-out). The logical operators && and || short-circuit (since 2019.05) and return boolean true/false rather than the operand (VERIFY); ! returns a boolean. Type-test builtins (all 2019.05 except is_function, 2021.01): is_undef, is_num (false for nan), is_bool, is_string, is_list (true for [] and any vector, false for ranges and strings), is_function. There is no typeof() and no is_range — a range is detectable only by elimination.
edge_cases: Truthiness table, falsy side exactly five values: false, 0 (and -0), "" (empty string), [] (empty vector), undef. Everything else truthy: "false", "0", " ", [0], [[]], [false], -1, inf, and nan (the toBool test is a plain != 0; nan != 0 is true). VERIFY: range values and function values as conditions — believed truthy; pin.

Type-mismatch arithmetic yields undef + WARNING and continues: "a"+1, [1]+2, true+1, "a"+"b" (no string concatenation via + — str() is the only concatenation). VERIFY exact warning format, believed like 'WARNING: undefined operation (string + number)' with file/line.

Vector addition has NO broadcasting: [1,2]+1 is undef with warning; [1,2]+[1,2,3] is undef with warning ('+'/'-' require equal lengths, applied recursively to nested vectors). Meanwhile '*' is shape-dispatched: vector*vector is a DOT PRODUCT (scalar), matrix*vector/vector*matrix/matrix*matrix are defined; elementwise multiply does not exist.
== is deep structural: [1,[2,"x"]] == [1,[2,"x"]] is true; [1,2] == [1,2,3] is false; 1 == "1" is false; 1 == true is false; undef == false is false; undef == undef is TRUE.

nan: nan == nan is false; nan != nan is true; all relationals involving nan are false; is_num(nan) is false (a documented carve-out in is_num, NOT in truthiness); nan is TRUTHY as a condition; echo prints nan. Obtain nan via 0/0.
VERIFY: [nan] == [nan] — believed false (elementwise comparison hits nan != nan); pin, libraries occasionally depend on vector equality.
VERIFY: range equality — [0:1:5] == [0:1:5] believed true (component compare of begin/step/end); a range never equals its expanded vector (different types, so false).
VERIFY: equality between function values — behavior unpinned (identity? always false? undef?); probe before promising anything.

Relational operators on anything but number-number or string-string yield undef: [1,2] < [1,3] is undef; undef < 1 is undef; mixed "1" < 2 is undef. VERIFY: whether a WARNING accompanies relational-mismatch undef, and specifically whether bool < bool is defined or undef (believed undef).
String ordering is lexicographic by Unicode code point (not locale, not bytes): "Z" < "a" is true (90 < 97).
is_num(inf) — VERIFY, believed true (inf is a number; only nan is excluded).
is_list: true for [] and any vector regardless of content; FALSE for strings, ranges, undef.
is_undef(never_defined_name) probes without emitting the unknown-variable warning; bare use of the same name warns and yields undef.
No is_range and no typeof: detecting a range requires elimination (not num/bool/string/list/undef/function). Keep this gap — do not add helpfully.

Indexing: v[i] with negative, non-integer, or out-of-range i yields undef (no Python negative indexing, no wrap). VERIFY: believed silent undef (no warning) for out-of-range — pin, and VERIFY that integer-valued doubles index correctly (v[1.0] works, v[1.5] undef).
String indexing s[i] yields a ONE-CHARACTER STRING (there is no character type); out-of-range undef. len(s) counts Unicode code points, not bytes.

Swizzles v.x/v.y/v.z (2019.05+) read elements 0/1/2 of a vector; on a too-short vector the missing component is undef; on non-vectors undef (VERIFY warning). Only x/y/z exist — no .w, no compound swizzles.
len() on non-list/non-string (numbers, booleans, ranges, undef) yields undef. VERIFY whether a warning accompanies it.

&& and || short-circuit only since 2019.05 (earlier releases evaluated both sides — old code has guard idioms shaped by that); they return boolean true/false, not the last operand (VERIFY — seed flags this). The ternary is lazy on the untaken branch and is THE recursion terminator.
Strings are iterable despite not being lists: [for (c="abc") c] gives ["a","b","c"]; each "ab" splices characters. VERIFY version coverage of string iteration in the statement-level for module.
Vectors are heterogeneous and nested arbitrarily: [1, "a", [true, [0:2]]] is legal; deep equality recurses through all of it.
undef propagation is per-operation: each mismatched operation emits its own WARNING; the GUI console may rate-limit duplicate lines (app behavior, not language semantics).

Snapshot-only: object values (from textmetrics()/fontmetrics(), behind --enable=textmetrics) with dot access and is_object(); absent in 2021.01 — is_object is an unknown function there (warning + undef).
impl_notes: Implement Value as a tagged union with exactly these variants; resist normalizing (no int fast-path leaking into semantics, no bool-number coercion). Two comparison code paths: total structural == and partial IEEE/lexicographic ordering. Route every mismatch through a single warn-and-return-undef helper so warning text/count is centralized and --hardwarnings can hook it. Oracle probes: warning text for each mismatch class, relational-mismatch warning presence, bool ordering, range/function equality, [nan]==[nan], is_num(inf), out-of-range index warning silence, &&/|| return type. The truthiness set and == totality are frozen contracts — test each listed literal.

name: Numbers & output formatting
summary: Every number is an IEEE-754 double; all angles everywhere are degrees; echo/str format numbers %g-style with 6 significant digits (so large integers go scientific and get rounded, and float error is hidden); domain errors and type mismatches produce nan/undef with WARNINGs instead of halting; the exact set and text of warnings is compatibility surface because --hardwarnings promotes any warning to a fatal error.

params.name: number representation
params.desc: f64 only — no integer type, no bignum; integer-looking values are doubles and lose exactness silently past 2^53.

params.name: numeric literals
params.desc: Decimal and exponent forms (1.5, 1e-3); NO hex/binary/octal; no literals for inf or nan (they arise from arithmetic only).

params.name: degrees convention
params.desc: sin/cos/tan take degrees; asin/acos/atan/atan2 return degrees; rotate, linear_extrude twist, rotate_extrude angle, $vpr, $vpf are degrees. Nothing in the language uses radians.

params.name: %g formatter
params.desc: echo and str() render numbers like printf %g with 6 significant digits: trailing zeros trimmed, integers without decimal point, scientific notation once the exponent leaves the %g window.

params.name: PI
params.desc: The only numeric constant (full double precision; echoes as 3.14159). There is no E — users write exp(1).

params.name: --hardwarnings
params.desc: CLI/preferences mode that turns the FIRST warning into a fatal error; CI pipelines rely on it, making the warning set itself part of the contract.

semantics: Arithmetic is plain IEEE-754 double arithmetic with these language-level decorations: division by zero warns ('WARNING: division by zero') and yields inf/-inf (0/0 yields nan); modulo is C fmod (result sign follows the dividend; x % 0 is nan); domain errors in sqrt/ln/log/asin/acos produce nan with a WARNING (since 2019.05; silently nan before). Nothing numeric ever throws — evaluation continues with inf/nan/undef flowing onward. All trigonometry is in degrees, and multiples of 30 and 45 degrees are special-cased to exact results in every quadrant (sin(180) == 0 exactly, cos(60) == 0.5; introduced 2019.05), which golden echo-based tests will expose. The observable text surface: echo prints 'ECHO: ' plus arguments joined by ', '; numbers are formatted double-conversion-style (6 significant digits, unpadded exponents — see the number formatting entry) with 6 SIGNIFICANT digits — 1/3 prints 0.333333, PI prints 3.14159, 10.0 prints 10 (no decimal point), 1234567 prints 1.23457e+6 (large integers go scientific AND get rounded — a famous trap), values below 1e-5 print scientific with an unpadded exponent ('1.5e-6'); 1.5e-5 itself prints fixed as '0.000015', inf prints inf, nan prints nan. str() uses the IDENTICAL formatter, so user string-building inherits the 6-digit rounding; 0.1+0.2 both echoes and str()s as 0.3, hiding float error. Diagnostics follow fixed shapes — 'WARNING: <message>, in file <path>, line <N>.', 'ERROR: ...', 'DEPRECATED: ...', and assert failures with 'TRACE: called by ...' stack lines — and are parsed by users, test suites, and tooling, so the strings must match the oracle verbatim. Because --hardwarnings turns any warning fatal, emitting too many warnings breaks scripts as surely as emitting too few.
edge_cases: Large integers in echo go scientific and ROUNDED: echo(1234567) prints 1.23457e+6; echo(123456) prints 123456; the cutover is at 1e6 (1000000 prints 1e+6, 999999 prints 999999) with unpadded exponents.
echo hides float error: 0.1+0.2 prints 0.3; 6-significant-digit rounding applies inside vectors too ([1/3] prints [0.333333]).
str() formats numbers exactly like echo — str(1e7) is "1e+7"; any user code building filenames/labels from big numbers inherits this. The two must share one formatter implementation.
Integers print without decimal point: 10.0 prints 10; 2.0*5 prints 10.
-0: echo prints '0' (UNIQUE_ZERO in the 2021.01 double-conversion formatter); 0 == -0 is true; sign(-0) is 0; the sign shows only via arithmetic (1/-0 == -inf).
inf prints 'inf', nan prints 'nan'; VERIFY -inf prints '-inf'. There are no literals; 1/0 (with warning) is the accessible source of inf, 0/0 of nan.

1/0 yields inf with 'WARNING: division by zero'; -1/0 yields -inf; VERIFY whether 0/0 emits the same division-by-zero warning text (result nan); x % 0 yields nan (VERIFY its warning, believed 'WARNING: modulo by zero' or the division text — pin).

Domain errors yield nan with WARNING since 2019.05: sqrt(-1), ln(-1), log(-1), asin(2), acos(-2). VERIFY per-function warning texts. VERIFY ln(0)/log(0) — believed -inf (C behavior), possibly with warning.

Exact trig: sin(180)==0 exactly (not 1.22e-16), cos(90)==0, tan(45)==1 — and 30/45/60 in every quadrant (sin(30)==0.5, cos(60)==0.5, tan(60)==sqrt(3)) via the degree-trig special cases introduced in 2019.05. Settled; matches the sin/cos/tan entries.
round() is half-away-from-zero: round(2.5) == 3, round(-2.5) == -3 — VERIFY against the oracle since C round vs rint differ and implementations vary.
% is fmod, sign follows dividend: 5%3 == 2, -5%3 == -2, 5%-3 == 2; fractional moduli work (5.5%2 == 1.5).

^ exponentiation is NEW in 2021.01 (pow() is the older spelling): right-associative (2^3^2 == 512); VERIFY precedence vs unary minus (-2^2 believed -4, i.e. ^ binds tighter than unary minus); VERIFY 0^0 (believed 1, C pow); negative base with non-integer exponent yields nan.
min()/max(): 2+ scalar args or a single vector arg; empty vector yields WARNING + undef; VERIFY behavior with non-numeric elements (believed undef/nan propagation — pin).
No unary-plus certainty: VERIFY whether '+5' parses (believed the grammar accepts unary +; pin, since it affects expression parsing compatibility).
VERIFY numeric literal corners: leading-dot '.5' and trailing-dot '5.' acceptance; exponent forms 1E3/1e+3. No hex (0x10 is a syntax error), no binary/octal.
Precision loss is silent past 2^53: echo(2^53 == 2^53+1) prints true; no warning exists for it.
Locale independence: the decimal separator is always '.', never ',', regardless of system locale; no digit grouping.

Diagnostic formats to clone verbatim (capture from oracle): 'WARNING: <msg>, in file <path>, line <N>.', 'ERROR: ...', 'DEPRECATED: ...', assert: ERROR: Assertion '(<condition source text>)' failed[: <message>] in file <path>, line <N>, then 'TRACE: called by '<module>', in file ..., line ...' lines unwinding the module stack. VERIFY exact punctuation of each.

The warning SET is surface (compatibility-critical under --hardwarnings): variable reassignment, unknown variable, undefined operation/type mismatch, unequal-length vector +/-, scalar+vector, division by zero, deprecated reversed range, $fa/$fs clamp, unknown named parameter, empty min/max, range step problems, deprecations (assign, triangles=), unknown module/function call. VERIFY completeness by diffing against oracle runs of a warning-torture script.
Warning/echo emission order is depth-first instantiation order, before/independent of geometry evaluation; duplicate-warning rate limiting in the GUI console is app behavior, not language.

Dev snapshots have been moving echo toward full-precision shortest-roundtrip number output — 2021.01 is firmly 6-significant-digit double-conversion output; VERIFY per-snapshot before chasing snapshot parity.

version() returns [2021, 1] style vectors (two elements on release builds; a third day element only on date-versioned snapshots) and version_num() returns 20210100-style numbers — these numbers flow through the same formatter rules when echoed (20210100 prints as 2.02101e+7!).
impl_notes: Write ONE number-formatting routine that both echo and str() call and freeze it against oracle output for a battery of magnitudes (10^-7..10^9, negative, -0, inf, nan, 6-digit boundary values like 999999.5). Implement warnings through a single channel with a --hardwarnings escalation switch. Pin via oracle probes: the %g cutover boundaries, -0, round() ties, ^ precedence vs unary minus, 0^0, x%0 warning, ln(0), every domain-error warning text, unary plus, and the exact-trig angle set and introduction release. Do not use platform printf %g blindly — verify it matches OpenSCAD's output for the boundary cases (it is believed to literally be %g, but freeze by test, not assumption).

name: Geometry model
summary: Geometry exists only in the instantiation tree, never as a value; every multi-statement grouping (top level, module bodies, blocks, transform children, for iterations) is an implicit union; 2D geometry lives at z=0 and may never mix with 3D in one boolean; and the language has two observable evaluation pipelines — approximate GPU preview (F5/OpenCSG, governed by convexity, $preview=true) and exact render (F6/CGAL) — whose differences (%, #, color(), late manifold errors) are part of the compatibility surface.

params.name: implicit union
params.desc: Any point where multiple geometry statements share a scope — top level, module bodies, { } blocks, if/for/let bodies, children of a transform — implicitly unions them. intersection_for exists precisely because wrapping for in intersection() intersects one pre-unioned blob.

params.name: dimensionality
params.desc: Every node is 2D or 3D. Booleans/hull/minkowski require uniform dimensionality; linear_extrude/rotate_extrude accept only 2D and produce 3D; projection accepts only 3D and produces 2D. These are the only bridges.

params.name: convexity
params.desc: Accepted on polyhedron, polygon, linear_extrude, rotate_extrude, surface, import, render, minkowski, resize, ...: 'max front-facing surfaces a ray can cross'. Affects ONLY OpenCSG preview correctness, never exported geometry — must be parsed everywhere, may be ignored by an always-exact engine.

params.name: $preview
params.desc: true in F5 preview / --preview PNG export, false in F6 render / mesh exports (2019.05+). Scripts branch on it; an implementation must set it coherently for its own pipeline.

params.name: modifiers * ! # %
params.desc: Parser-level prefixes on one instantiation: * disables the subtree everywhere; ! makes it the only evaluated subtree (ancestor transforms still apply); # includes it in results but tints it pink in preview; % shows it gray in preview but EXCLUDES it from render/CSG/exports.

params.name: render()
params.desc: Semantically the identity; forces exact geometry for its subtree even during preview (the classic OpenCSG-artifact workaround). hull(), minkowski(), and resize() also force child geometry evaluation.

params.name: geometry caches
params.desc: OpenSCAD memoizes evaluated geometry per identical subtree (GeometryCache/CGALCache); repeated instantiations of the same module with the same arguments must be cache hits — a de facto performance contract.

semantics: OpenSCAD scripts do not compute geometry values; they INSTANTIATE a tree. Statements and expressions are disjoint grammars: 'x = cube(1);' is a syntax error, modules are not first-class (only function values are, since 2021.01), and geometry can never be stored, compared, or measured from the language (resize/hull react to geometry internally, but no measurement is exposed to expressions). Instantiation happens depth-first; echo/assert/warnings fire during instantiation, before geometry evaluation, and their order is observable. Every grouping construct implicitly unions its children — top level, module bodies, { } blocks, if branches, let bodies, for iterations (hence intersection_for), and the children of transforms. 2D geometry is dimensionally 2D in the CSG tree, conceptually at z=0; preview draws it as a thin slab (visual convention only). Mixing 2D and 3D children in union/difference/intersection/hull/minkowski is an ERROR ('Mixing 2D and 3D objects is not supported'); linear_extrude and rotate_extrude are the only 2D-to-3D bridges and projection() the only 3D-to-2D bridge. Two pipelines exist in the reference implementation: F5 preview composes CSG approximately on the GPU via OpenCSG (accuracy bounded by each node's convexity parameter) with $preview=true, while F6 render computes exact meshes via CGAL (Manifold in 2023+ snapshots) with $preview=false. Preview-vs-render differences are language surface: % subtrees appear (translucent gray) only in preview and are excluded from render and every export; # subtrees are highlighted pink in preview but fully included in render/exports; * removes a subtree everywhere; ! restricts evaluation to one subtree (with its ancestor transform chain); color() affects only preview output in 2021.01; non-manifold polyhedra/imports frequently succeed in preview and only fail at render; render() forces exactness locally. An always-exact reimplementation must still emulate the observable semantics: flip $preview appropriately, honor %/#/!/* per-pipeline behavior, and accept convexity everywhere. The 2D subsystem runs in a separate fixed-point polygon-clipping kernel (Clipper) whose quantization differs from the 3D pipeline — micro-scale 2D precision behavior is not the same as 3D.
edge_cases: Implicit-union sites, exhaustively: file top level, module bodies, { } blocks, if/else branch bodies, for and intersection_for iteration bodies (for unions ITERATIONS; intersection_for intersects them), let statement bodies, and multi-child transform/boolean arguments. Wrapping for in intersection() does NOT intersect iterations — it intersects the single already-unioned result (the reason intersection_for exists).

'x = cube(1);' is a syntax/semantic error: instantiations are statements, not expressions. VERIFY the exact parser error text. Likewise modules cannot be passed, stored, or returned (no module literals in any stable release).

Mixing 2D and 3D in any boolean/hull/minkowski: ERROR 'Mixing 2D and 3D objects is not supported'. VERIFY exact prefix/casing and whether it aborts the whole compile or just that subtree (believed: subtree yields empty and an ERROR is logged — pin).
VERIFY: a 2D and a 3D object both at top level — believed to hit the same implicit-union mixing error at F6/export while F5 may draw both; pin the behavior per pipeline.
linear_extrude/rotate_extrude with a 3D child: ERROR (VERIFY text); projection with a 2D child: VERIFY (believed warning/ignore or error — pin).

2D is drawn in preview as a thin slab (historically ~1 unit tall visual); this is cosmetic — the tree node is 2D and exports as 2D only. Exporting 2D to STL or 3D to DXF/SVG errors: VERIFY texts, approx 'Current top level object is not a 3D object' / '...not a 2D object'.
Exporting an empty top-level result is an error: VERIFY text (approx 'ERROR: Nothing to export' or 'No top level geometry to render').

Degenerate primitives (cube(0), cylinder(h=0), circle(-1)) emit WARNING and contribute empty geometry; evaluation continues. Empty children: union ignores them; difference with empty FIRST child yields empty; difference minus empty subtrahends is unchanged; intersection with any empty child yields empty. VERIFY minkowski with an empty child — behavior changed across versions (warning-and-ignore vs empty result); pin for 2021.01.

Modifier semantics per pipeline: % = preview-visible (translucent gray), EXCLUDED from render/CSG/exports; # = preview-highlighted (translucent red/pink), INCLUDED in render/exports; * = excluded everywhere; ! = only that subtree evaluated, ancestor transforms still applied. Modifiers compose (%*, #translate(...)); VERIFY resolution when multiple ! appear (believed the first one encountered wins) and nested ! inside a !-subtree.
% and # inside hull()/minkowski(): inner modifiers/colors are dropped by these operations. VERIFY exact interaction (e.g. hull() over a % child).

color() is preview-only in 2021.01: F6 render, STL/OFF/AMF/3MF exports drop it. Snapshots with the Manifold backend carry color through render and into 3MF export — a deliberate divergence to gate behind a feature flag.

Non-manifold or self-intersecting polyhedron()/import() geometry typically previews fine and only fails at F6 with CGAL errors. Do NOT promise cloning CGAL's error strings — promise detection timing (validity enforced at exact-evaluation time, not instantiation time).

convexity is accepted (and geometrically inert) wherever listed; wrong/low convexity in OpenSCAD produces EXPECTED preview artifacts in difference()-heavy models (the render()-wrapping folk fix). An always-exact implementation simply never shows the artifacts — an accepted, user-visible improvement, but it must still parse convexity everywhere.

render(convexity) is the identity on geometry; must be accepted with children of either dimensionality. VERIFY: render() of 2D children passes 2D through (believed yes, with the result cached as polygons).

Geometry caching is a de facto contract: a for loop stamping the same module 1000x must evaluate its mesh once (OpenSCAD keys caches on the subtree identity). Without memoization, real-world scripts (recursive trees, grids) run orders of magnitude slower — treat as required. VERIFY cache-key semantics only if exposing cache controls.

lazy-union (experimental, 2021.01+, --enable=lazy-union): removes the TOP-LEVEL implicit union so multiple top-level solids export as separate objects (multi-object 3MF). Off by default; decide whether to mirror the flag.

2D pipeline quantization: booleans/offset run through Clipper-style fixed-point clipping with its own coordinate grid; results at micrometer scales differ from the float 3D pipeline. Observable in vertex coordinates of exported SVG/DXF. VERIFY the effective quantum (Clipper integer scale factor) if promising coordinate-exact 2D output.

Tessellation phase contracts (observable in every export): circle = INSCRIBED polygon, first vertex at angle 0 on +X, CCW; sphere = N meridians with ceil(N/2) latitude rings at half-step phase offsets (no pole vertices); cylinder = fragment 0 at +X, count from max(r1,r2); rotate_extrude seam fixed at the +X half-plane. Real models (hex nuts via $fn=6, r/cos(180/n) hole compensation) depend on these — clone exactly.

polyhedron() faces wind CLOCKWISE viewed from outside (reverse of STL/OBJ convention); polygon() holes come from nested paths (even-odd/nesting rule — pin exact overlap semantics); both defer validity errors to exact-evaluation time.

echo/assert/warning emission happens at instantiation (depth-first, pre-geometry); console order is observable surface. Geometry evaluation order behind it is not observable except through timing and cache effects.

The .csg export is a flattened normal form of the instantiated tree (transforms/booleans/primitives with resolved parameters) — the single best differential-testing oracle format; AST export reproduces parsed source; ECHO export captures the console stream.

Coordinate system: right-handed, +Z up in the default view, unitless (conventionally mm). scale() with negative factors mirrors and can invert face orientation — the exact kernel must handle inverted winding. VERIFY behavior of scale([1,1,0]) on 3D geometry at render time (degenerate — believed CGAL error or empty; pin).
impl_notes: Model the pipeline distinction explicitly even in a single always-exact engine: a boolean 'preview mode' flag drives $preview, % inclusion, # tinting, and color() visibility; keep the render-time result of a %-subtree out of every export path. Accept-and-ignore convexity via a shared parameter table. Implement subtree-identity geometry memoization from day one (hash of node type + resolved params + child hashes). Oracle probes: mixing-error text and per-pipeline behavior, multiple-! resolution, minkowski-empty-child, 2D/3D top-level mixing, export-dimension error texts, empty-export error, scale-to-zero at render. Use .csg export diffing as the primary compatibility harness before any mesh comparison.

name: Ranges
signature:
r = [0:2:10];          // begin : step : end — a range VALUE, not a vector
echo(r);               // ECHO: [0 : 2 : 10]
for (i = r) echo(i);   // 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10
echo([ each [3:-1:1] ]);   // [3, 2, 1]
for (i = [4:1]) echo(i);   // DEPRECATED reversed range: still iterates 1..4
summary: [begin:end] (implicit step 1) and [begin:step:end] construct a range — a distinct lazy value type (is_list false, len undef, indexing undef) consumed by for, intersection_for, each, list comprehensions, and children(); iteration runs begin, begin+step, ... while within end; negative steps descend; and the legacy quirk that [begin:end] with begin>end is silently swapped (with a deprecation warning) must be cloned.

params.name: begin
params.desc: First value produced. Any numeric expression; non-numeric/nan bounds make the range degenerate (warning — VERIFY exact behavior).

params.name: step
params.desc: Increment; omitted in the two-part form (defaults to 1). Negative steps produce descending iteration; step 0 is invalid (WARNING; yields no/limited iteration — VERIFY exact result).

params.name: end
params.desc: Inclusive bound: values are produced while they have not passed end in the direction of step; whether a float-accumulated endpoint is included depends on the exact count formula — pin via oracle.

semantics: A range literal uses colon syntax inside square brackets and produces a value of the distinct range type: it is NOT a vector — is_list returns false, len returns undef, indexing returns undef — and no builtin converts it to a list except iteration ([each r] or [for (i=r) i]). Ranges are consumed lazily by the for module, intersection_for, list-comprehension for, each, and children(): a huge range like [0:1e9] iterates without materializing a billion-element vector (memory is only committed when a comprehension or each collects results). Iteration semantics: values begin, begin+step, begin+2*step, ... are produced while they do not pass end (ascending for positive step, descending for negative); end is inclusive when landed on exactly, but with fractional steps floating-point error decides whether the endpoint is reached — the element-count rule must be pinned bit-for-bit against the oracle (e.g. whether [0:0.1:1] produces 10 or 11 values). The two-part form [b:e] has implicit step 1, and carries the notorious legacy rule: when begin > end, 2021.01 SWAPS the bounds, emits 'DEPRECATED: Using ranges of the form [begin:end] with begin value greater than the end value is deprecated.', and iterates ascending anyway. Echo prints ranges with spaced colons in three-part form, e.g. [0 : 2 : 10].
edge_cases: Range is a distinct type: is_list(r) false, is_num(r) false, len(r) undef (VERIFY accompanying warning), r[0] undef, .x undef. Detection is only by elimination — there is no is_range.
echo/str rendering: [0:2:10] prints as '[0 : 2 : 10]' (spaces around colons). VERIFY: whether the two-part form [0:5] prints its implicit step (believed yes, as '[0 : 1 : 5]') — pin exact text.

Legacy reversed range: [10:1] emits 'DEPRECATED: Using ranges of the form [begin:end] with begin value greater than the end value is deprecated.' and iterates 1..10 ASCENDING (bounds swapped) in 2021.01. VERIFY: newer snapshots have discussed treating it as empty — pin per targeted version.
VERIFY: whether the swap applies to the explicit-step form — believed NOT: [10:1:0] (positive step, begin>end) yields ZERO iterations with no deprecation message; only the two-part form swaps. Pin.
Negative step: [10:-2:0] produces 10,8,6,4,2,0. Negative step with begin < end ([0:-1:5]) produces zero iterations. VERIFY whether any warning accompanies the empty case (believed silent).
Step 0: WARNING and no usable iteration. VERIFY exact text and result (believed the range yields nothing; older versions differed) — clone the 2021.01 behavior.

Fractional steps accumulate float error: [0:0.1:1] endpoint inclusion is decided by the internal count formula, not by exact arithmetic — VERIFY the produced count and the exact values (whether iteration computes begin + i*step or accumulates val += step changes the low bits of every produced value; pin which one 2021.01 uses).

VERIFY: internal element-count formula (believed of the form floor((end-begin)/step)+1 evaluated in doubles, clamped at 0) and any epsilon handling — this single formula decides every off-by-one dispute; freeze it with oracle probes at boundary values like [0:0.1:0.3], [1:1/3:2], [0:0.7:7].

Huge ranges: for(i=[0:1e9]) iterates lazily (slow, no memory blowup); [each [0:1e9]] and comprehensions materialize and will exhaust memory. VERIFY: whether 2021.01 imposes any hard cap or warning on range element count (believed a clamp exists at the uint32 boundary internally; probe [0:1e10] and nan/inf bounds — approx 'WARNING: Bad range parameter').

Non-numeric components: [0:undef:5], ["a":1:5], nan/inf as begin/step/end — VERIFY behavior (believed WARNING and a degenerate range producing nothing; inf end producing effectively unbounded iteration must be probed carefully).
Ranges as children() selectors: children([0:2]) instantiates children 0,1,2 — ranges work anywhere the implementation iterates indices. Out-of-range values follow children()'s own error rules.
Range equality: VERIFY [0:1:5] == [0:1:5] (believed true, comparing begin/step/end structurally) and whether the swapped legacy form compares equal to its normalized form (probe [5:1] == [1:5]).
A range never == a vector, even one with identical elements (different types compare false).
Ranges in boolean context: VERIFY truthiness (believed truthy like any non-listed value, even when producing zero iterations).

for over a range binds plain numbers; the loop variable in fractional ranges carries accumulated float representation — i == 0.3 comparisons against range-produced values are unreliable in user code, and your implementation must reproduce the same bit patterns as the oracle's iteration strategy.
String/vector iteration is a separate for-capability, not ranges: for (c = "abc") and for (v = [[1,2],[3,4]]) — do not funnel through range machinery. A bare scalar iterates once (VERIFY, per seed).

Ranges may be stored in variables, passed to functions/modules, put in vectors ([[0:5], [10:20]] is a vector of two ranges), and passed through $-variables — they are ordinary values apart from their lazy consumption.
example:
r = [0:2:10];
echo(r, is_list(r), len(r));   // ECHO: [0 : 2 : 10], false, undef
for (i = r) echo(i);            // 0 2 4 6 8 10
echo([ each [3:-1:1] ]);        // ECHO: [3, 2, 1]
echo([ for (i = [0:0.1:0.3]) i ]);  // pin endpoint inclusion vs oracle
for (i = [4:1]) echo("legacy", i);  // DEPRECATED warning, iterates 1..4
cube(1);
impl_notes: Represent as {begin, step, end} doubles with normalization applied ONLY for the two-part begin>end form (swap + deprecation). Implement one canonical count/iteration routine shared by for, each, comprehensions, and children(), and freeze it against oracle probes: fractional-step endpoint cases, begin+i*step vs accumulation bit patterns, step 0, negative-step empty, nan/inf bounds, huge-count clamping, and the echo text including implicit-step display. Keep iteration lazy in for and eager only at collection points. The reversed-range swap is bug-for-bug required for 2021.01; gate any snapshot 'empty' behavior behind a version flag.

name: Recursion & evaluation limits
summary: With no loops-with-state, recursion is the language's only general computation mechanism: the lazy ternary is the sole terminator; functions get tail-call elimination since 2019.05 (deep tail recursion into the millions must work because libraries rely on it) while non-tail recursion is stack-bounded; modules hit a fixed 'Recursion detected' error at a set depth; and assert() is the only construct that halts evaluation.

params.name: cond ? a : b
params.desc: The ternary is lazy on the untaken branch and right-associative — it is THE recursion terminator. An eager-ternary implementation infinite-loops every recursive library function.
Short-circuit since 2019.05 (both sides were evaluated before that — old code's guard idioms reflect it); usable as auxiliary recursion guards but the ternary is the primary one.

params.name: tail-call elimination
params.desc: Since 2019.05, a function whose recursive call is in tail position reuses the frame; recursion depth on the order of 1,000,000 is expected to work.

params.name: module recursion limit
params.desc: Modules recurse via self-instantiation; exceeding the implementation's depth limit raises an error naming the module, approx "ERROR: Recursion detected calling module 'name'".

params.name: assert(cond, message)
params.desc: The only halting construct: on failure, evaluation stops with an ERROR naming the condition's source text (plus optional message) and TRACE: lines unwinding the module call stack.

semantics: OpenSCAD has no while, break, continue, return, or mutation; every algorithm is a single-expression function using the ternary for termination and recursion for iteration, or a data-driven for/comprehension. Laziness rules make this viable: the ternary evaluates only the taken branch, and && / || short-circuit (2019.05+). Function recursion comes in two regimes. Calls in TAIL position are eliminated (2019.05+): 'f(n, acc) = n<=0 ? acc : f(n-1, acc+n)' runs at depths around a million — the BOSL2-class libraries build sort/map/fold on this and an implementation without TCO (or an equivalent trampoline) fails them immediately. Non-tail recursion ('n + sum(n-1)') consumes real evaluator stack and is bounded; exceeding the bound produces a recursion error naming the function rather than a crash. Module recursion (a module instantiating itself, usually guarded by if) is legal and idiomatic for fractals/trees, but is bounded by a fixed depth check with an explicit error approx "ERROR: Recursion detected calling module 'name'". Errors and limits are observable surface: the recursion error texts, the assert() failure format with its TRACE stack unwind, and the practical depth thresholds all get exercised by real scripts and test suites. Nothing else halts: warnings (including under-recursion type mismatches) let evaluation continue; only assert() failure — and fatal errors like recursion detection — stop the run.
edge_cases: The ternary MUST be lazy: 'f(n) = n<=0 ? 0 : f(n-1)' with eager branches recurses forever. Right-associativity: 'a ? b : c ? d : e' parses as 'a ? b : (c ? d : e)' — the else-if chain idiom.

&& and || short-circuit only since 2019.05; pre-2019.05 scripts could not rely on 'n>0 && f(n-1)' as a guard. 2021.01 semantics: short-circuiting, returning booleans (VERIFY return type, see Type chapter).

VERIFY: the exact set of tail positions eligible for TCO — the ternary's taken branch certainly; believed also the body of let() expressions and the trailing subexpression of echo(...) expr and assert(...) expr wrappers; probe each (a library that traces with echo inside a tail call must not lose TCO).
Deep tail recursion contract: on the order of 1,000,000 frames must complete (the seed pins 'into the millions'). VERIFY the practical ceiling on the official 2021.01 binary and match or exceed it.

Non-tail function recursion is stack-bounded with an error naming the function: VERIFY exact text (believed "ERROR: Recursion detected calling function 'f'") and the practical depth (platform stack dependent in the C++ implementation — thousands to tens of thousands; pin the oracle's observed depth and document yours).

Module recursion limit: VERIFY exact error text (believed "ERROR: Recursion detected calling module 'name'") and the depth at which it fires; the seed calls it 'a fixed recursion depth limit'. After the error, VERIFY whether evaluation aborts entirely or the subtree is dropped (believed fatal for the compile).
Mutual recursion (a calls b calls a) hits the same machinery for both functions and modules; the error names the module/function whose re-entry tripped the check — VERIFY which name appears.
Recursion through children(): a module that passes children back into itself recurses through the instantiation stack the same way; $parent_modules/parent_module(n) observe the stack depth.
Genuinely infinite TAIL recursion is not detected — it runs until the user kills it (or memory is exhausted by accumulated data). Do not add a helpful cap; scripts distinguish 'slow' from 'error'.

C-style comprehension loops [for (init; cond; update) expr] can also loop forever if cond never fails. VERIFY: whether 2021.01 imposes any iteration cap or warning on generator-for loops (believed uncapped — probe; if a cap exists, clone its threshold and message).

Deeply nested expressions (parentheses, vector literals) can exhaust the PARSER's stack separately from evaluation: VERIFY 2021.01 behavior on pathological nesting (believed crash-or-error at platform-dependent depth; your parser should error gracefully at a documented depth).

assert(false) halts with: ERROR: Assertion '(false)' failed in file <path>, line <N> — with an optional ': <message>' (message formatted like an echo value) and then 'TRACE: called by '<module>', in file ..., line ...' lines for each module stack frame, innermost first. VERIFY exact punctuation and frame order; test suites parse these.
The expression form 'assert(cond, msg) expr' (2019.05+) evaluates to expr on success — it sits INSIDE function bodies and participates in tail-position analysis (VERIFY).

Errors during recursion (type mismatch producing undef, division by zero) do NOT stop recursion — they warn and continue, so a buggy terminator comparing against undef can still run to the depth limit. The resulting warning flood is observable behavior (GUI may rate-limit display).

Memoization: OpenSCAD does NOT memoize function calls — exponential naive-fib really is exponential. Do not add semantic-level function caching (echo side effects inside functions would be lost/reordered); geometry caching (see Geometry model) is separate and safe because instantiation echoes happen pre-cache. VERIFY: echo-expression inside a function called twice with same args prints twice.

Stack depth interacts with implementation platform: OpenSCAD's limits derive from the C-stack; a wasm32 build has a small shadow stack — implement the evaluator with an explicit heap stack or trampoline so YOUR limits are at least the oracle's, or deep libraries will trap where OpenSCAD succeeds.

Performance contracts adjacent to recursion: comprehension-built lists must be O(1) amortized append, and str()-based accumulation in deep recursion is O(n^2) unless rope-like — real libraries hit both.
impl_notes: Build the evaluator iteratively (explicit stack/trampoline) from the start — retrofitting TCO is painful. Tail-position analysis must cover ternary branches, let bodies, and echo/assert expression wrappers (verify each against the oracle first). Pin via oracle probes: exact 'Recursion detected' texts for module and function, observed depth ceilings for module recursion and non-tail function recursion, tail-recursion at 10^6, assert failure format including TRACE order, double-echo from repeated pure calls (proving no function memoization). Document your own limits where they exceed OpenSCAD's; never undercut them. Treat infinite tail loops as user responsibility — provide cancellation in the host app, not a semantic cap.

name: Determinism & compatibility posture
summary: The compatibility contract for a 2021.01 reimplementation: PROMISE full determinism (identical script and inputs give identical console output, warning set/order, and geometry), exact tessellation/fragment-formula parity, and mesh-level (solid) equivalence with OpenSCAD 2021.01; NEVER promise byte-identical STL/vertex ordering versus the official binary or across versions, cloned CGAL error strings, or bit-compatible seeded rands(); report version()=[2021,1]/version_num()=20210100 so libraries feature-detect correctly, and pin every uncertainty by differential testing against the official AppImage as an oracle.

params.name: version()
params.desc: Returns [year, month] on release builds ([year, month, day] on snapshots), e.g. [2021, 1]; libraries (BOSL2 etc.) feature-test on it, so the reported value gates which library code paths run.

params.name: version_num()
params.desc: Returns YYYYMMPP as a number, e.g. 20210100 — the more commonly tested form. Report 20210100 to claim the 2021.01 baseline.

params.name: oracle formats
params.desc: .csg (flattened instantiated tree), ECHO (console capture), AST exports from the official 2021.01 binary — the differential-testing ground truth for language semantics before any mesh comparison.

params.name: --enable=<feature> model
params.desc: OpenSCAD gates snapshot features behind explicit flags (lazy-union, manifold, roof, textmetrics); mirror this opt-in model rather than silently enabling snapshot behavior in a 2021.01-baseline implementation.

semantics: The contract has two tiers. Tier 1 — self-consistency (absolute): the implementation is a pure function of (script, file inputs, CLI defines, feature flags, $t/camera inputs): every run produces the identical echo/warning/error text in identical depth-first instantiation order, the identical geometry with identical vertex coordinates and identical vertex/triangle ordering, and identical export bytes. No hash-map iteration order, thread scheduling, locale, or wall clock may leak into results; geometry caching must be semantically invisible. Tier 2 — parity with OpenSCAD 2021.01: language-level observables should match the official binary verbatim (echo/str 6-significant-digit double-conversion formatting, warning texts and counts, deprecation and assert/TRACE formats, the fragment formula and tessellation phase contracts, search()'s ragged results, reversed-range swapping), because scripts, CI pipelines with --hardwarnings, and golden tests parse them. Geometry parity is promised at the SOLID level: the same point sets and volumes given the same tessellation contracts — primitive vertex positions should match to double precision since the tessellation formulas are pinned, but the triangulation of polygon interiors, the vertex/triangle ORDER in exports, and near-degenerate CSG outcomes follow kernel internals (CGAL in 2021.01, Manifold in snapshots) that OpenSCAD itself does not keep stable across versions. Therefore: never promise byte-identical STL against the official binary, never promise its internal error messages, and treat rands() bit-compatibility as out of scope unless std::mt19937 plus its distribution mapping is deliberately cloned (std::uniform_real_distribution is not even specified identically across C++ standard libraries). Report the 2021.01 version numbers, add snapshot features only behind explicit flags mirroring --enable, and convert every VERIFY item in this reference into an oracle-diff test before freezing semantics.
edge_cases: PROMISE: identical (script, inputs, version) yields identical console byte stream — echo text, warning set, warning ORDER (depth-first instantiation), and error/TRACE formats. Users' golden tests and MCP-layer parsers depend on it.

PROMISE: reproducible tessellation — the fragment formula, circle first-vertex-at-+X CCW inscribed contract, sphere half-step ring phase with no pole vertices, cylinder fragment phase, and rotate_extrude +X seam produce identical vertex coordinates run-to-run and match the oracle to double precision.

PROMISE: geometry caching, parallelism, and lazy evaluation are semantically invisible — cached and uncached runs byte-match; instantiation-time echoes fire identically regardless of geometry cache hits.

NEVER promise: byte-identical STL/OFF/AMF/3MF versus the official binary — CGAL's vertex/triangle ordering is internal and not stable even across OpenSCAD's own versions; promise mesh-level equivalence (same solid: matching vertex SET for primitives, matching volume/topology for CSG results) instead.
NEVER promise: identical triangulation of >3-vertex polyhedron faces, polygon()-with-holes interiors, or text() glyph tessellation — only that the resulting solids/regions are equivalent.

NEVER promise: cloned CGAL error/assertion strings on invalid geometry — promise the detection TIMING (failures surface at exact-evaluation/render, not instantiation) and a documented error of your own.

NEVER promise near-degenerate CSG parity: exactly-coincident faces, zero-thickness results, and epsilon-scale 2D features may legitimately differ from CGAL/Clipper outcomes; document as unspecified rather than chasing.

rands(): with a seed, reproducible WITHIN your implementation forever (freeze your PRNG); bit-matching OpenSCAD requires cloning std::mt19937 AND its uniform_real_distribution mapping — VERIFY: std::uniform_real_distribution output is not pinned by the C++ standard, so the official binary itself may differ across platform stdlibs; recommended posture is to NOT promise cross-implementation rands() equality. Unseeded rands() is nondeterministic by definition — the only sanctioned nondeterminism in the language.

version()/version_num() gate real library code paths (BOSL2 feature-detects): report [2021,1]/20210100 for baseline claims. VERIFY: what official snapshots report (snapshot date forms like [2025,x,y]) before emulating one. Note the echo trap: version_num() echoes as 2.02101e+7 under %g — comparisons work, display looks odd; clone as-is.

Echo number formatting is part of determinism surface: the 6-significant-digit double-conversion formatter must be frozen and shared by echo/str; snapshots moving to shortest-roundtrip output are a DIFFERENT contract — never mix behind the 2021.01 flag.

--hardwarnings parity: the exact SET of emitted warnings is a compatibility gate — an extra warning your implementation adds turns green CI runs red; a missing one hides bugs. Diff warning inventories against the oracle on a torture script and freeze.
$t and camera ($vpr/$vpt/$vpd/$vpf) are INPUTS: per-frame determinism given their values; animation runs are deterministic frame-by-frame.
Locale/platform independence: '.' decimal separator always; UTF-8 handling identical across platforms; no filesystem ordering leaks (e.g. font enumeration for text() must be deterministic or pinned).
Preview vs render divergence (%/#/color()/$preview) is deliberate, specified nondeterminism BETWEEN pipelines, never within one — each pipeline is individually deterministic.

Oracle methodology: use the official 2021.01 AppImage headless; compare (1) ECHO/console verbatim, (2) .csg export (flattened normal form — catches evaluator/tessellation-parameter divergence without mesh comparison), (3) mesh equivalence via volume/topology/vertex-set matching with tolerance, never byte-diff. Convert every VERIFY item in this reference into a pinned test before freezing.

Snapshot posture: add 2023+ features (manifold backend behavior, roof(), fill(), textmetrics objects, import/export additions, lazy-union) only behind explicit user-visible flags mirroring OpenSCAD's --enable names; never let a flagged feature alter unflagged 2021.01 behavior (including echo formatting and color-through-render).

Performance posture (expectation, not semantics): subtree geometry caching, O(1) amortized list building, and fast recursive functions are required for real scripts to complete; document that timing is never part of the compatibility promise.

Licensing constraint on methodology: the reference implementation is GPLv2+ and CGAL is GPL — a cleanroom reimplementation pins behavior via the CC BY-SA manual and BLACK-BOX oracle observation only; never port OpenSCAD/CGAL source. Manifold (Apache-2.0) and Clipper2 (BSL-1.0) algorithms/papers are safe references.
example:
echo(version(), version_num());   // ECHO: [2021, 1], 2.02101e+7
assert(version_num() >= 20210100);
r = rands(0, 1, 3, 42);            // seeded: reproducible per implementation
echo(r);                            // freeze YOUR values; don't promise OpenSCAD's
sphere(5, $fn=24);                  // vertex positions: promised; STL bytes: not
impl_notes: Engineer determinism structurally: ordered maps everywhere results can leak, a single frozen number formatter, deterministic ID/ordering for generated vertices, and cache designs proven invisible by cache-on/cache-off byte-diff tests in CI. Build the oracle harness first — script corpus, run official 2021.01 headless, capture ECHO/.csg/meshes, diff on every commit; promote each VERIFY item from this reference into that corpus. Freeze your seeded rands() stream as YOUR contract with a documented note that it diverges from OpenSCAD. Publish the compatibility statement in these exact tiers (self-consistency: byte-exact; OpenSCAD parity: console-verbatim + solid-equivalent; explicitly excluded: STL bytes, triangulation, CGAL errors, rands bits, timing) so users and downstream tests target the right guarantees.

name: child (deprecated)
summary: Legacy singular predecessor of children(). Deprecated when children() arrived (2014.03), but STILL registered and functional in 2021.01; removed only after 2021.01.

params.name: index
params.desc: 0-based index of the passed child to instantiate; omitted = first child.

semantics: Pre-2014 modules re-instantiated their passed subtree with child(). children() replaced it with range/index support in 2014.03. In 2021.01 child() still works: each call instantiates the indexed child and emits "DEPRECATED: child() will be removed in future releases. Use children() instead." Actual removal happened only after 2021.01.
edge_cases: Functional in 2021.01 with a per-call DEPRECATED message — VERIFY the exact text and whether it repeats per call or is deduplicated.
Migration is mechanical: child() -> children(0) / children(i).
since: pre-2015.03 (deprecated 2014.03; still functional in 2021.01; removed post-2021.01)
impl_notes: Implement as a deprecated alias of children() emitting the deprecation warning — 2021.01 parity requires it to work.

name: import_stl / import_dxf / import_off (deprecated)
summary: Deprecated per-format aliases of import(), from before the unified importer.

params.name: file
params.desc: Path, resolved like import().

semantics: Each behaves as import() restricted to one format. In 2021.01 all three still function as deprecated aliases, emitting the DEPRECATED-removal warning on every use; they were removed only after 2021.01. Scripts in the wild (pre-2014 Thingiverse era) still contain them.
edge_cases: Functional in 2021.01: each call emits 'DEPRECATED: The import_stl() module will be removed in future releases. Use import() instead.' — VERIFY the exact per-name message text.

None of the classic deprecations (child(), assign(), import_stl/import_dxf/import_off, dxf_linear_extrude/dxf_rotate_extrude, triangles=) was removed by the 2021.01 baseline — all remain deprecated-but-functional; removals came only after 2021.01.
since: pre-2015.03 (deprecated 2011.12, alongside the introduction of unified import())
impl_notes: Implement as aliases of import() that emit the deprecation warning — 2021.01 parity requires them to work, and old scripts then run unmodified.

name: textmetrics (snapshot)
signature: textmetrics(text, size, font, halign, valign, spacing, direction, language, script)
summary: SNAPSHOT-ONLY (--enable=textmetrics): returns an object describing the rendered extents of a text() call with the same arguments.

params.name: (all)
params.desc: Mirror text() parameters exactly.

semantics: Returns an object value with fields including position [x,y] (bounding-box origin), size [w,h], ascent, descent, offset [x,y], and advance [x,y] — the measurements needed to align or box text geometrically. This function is the reason the object type and is_object() exist.
edge_cases: Gated behind --enable=textmetrics in snapshots; absent in 2021.01 (unknown-function warning -> undef).
VERIFY: exact field set and coordinate conventions against a snapshot build before implementing.
Field access uses dot syntax: textmetrics(...).advance.
impl_notes: Implement alongside text() since both need the same font metrics; expose behind a feature flag mirroring upstream gating.

name: fontmetrics (snapshot)
summary: SNAPSHOT-ONLY (--enable=textmetrics): returns an object of font-wide vertical metrics at a given size.

params.name: size
params.desc: Em scaling as in text().

params.name: font
params.desc: Family[:style=] selector as in text().

semantics: Returns an object with nominal and max ascent/descent groups, interline spacing, and the resolved font family/style — font-wide values independent of any particular string.
edge_cases: Absent in 2021.01 (unknown-function warning -> undef).
VERIFY: exact field names (nominal.ascent etc.) against a snapshot build.
impl_notes: Same font-metric tables as text(); trivial once text() metrics exist.

name: object values & dot access (snapshot)
summary: SNAPSHOT-ONLY value type: an immutable string-keyed record returned by textmetrics()/fontmetrics(), read with dot access; tested by is_object().
semantics: Objects are not constructible from user syntax in snapshots (no literal form); they arrive only from builtins. Dot access on them generalizes the member-access operator beyond vector .x/.y/.z. is_object(x) tests the type; all other type tests return false on objects.
edge_cases: Baseline 2021.01 has NO object type: is_object is likewise snapshot-era, and dot access is only the vector .x/.y/.z swizzle.
VERIFY: equality semantics and echo/str rendering of objects on a snapshot build before promising any behavior.
Accessing a missing field: VERIFY — believed undef without warning.
impl_notes: Decide early whether your dialect ships objects at all; if yes, gate them behind the same feature flag and keep is_object() false-returning when disabled.

name: group
summary: Undocumented but real builtin: a pure grouping node that implicitly unions its children — the node OpenSCAD itself emits in .csg dumps for every block.
semantics: Semantically identical to an anonymous union of its children. Every { } child block, module body, and loop body appears as group() in exported .csg trees, so a .csg-diffing test harness must both emit and accept it. It is callable from user source, where it behaves as union() without being one (VERIFY: interaction with intersection_for and CSG normalization — believed identical to union).
edge_cases: Not in the documentation or cheat sheet; presence is observable via .csg export.
VERIFY: group() with modifier characters and in difference() subtrahend position — believed to behave exactly as union().
example: group(){ cube(1); sphere(1); } // same as union()
impl_notes: Implement as an alias of union and EMIT it in .csg dumps where OpenSCAD does — the .csg golden-diff harness depends on matching this wrapper structure.

name: feature flags & lazy-union (--enable)
summary: Snapshot features are gated per-run by --enable=<flag> (or Preferences > Features); one of them, lazy-union, changes core language semantics.
semantics: Flags relevant to a reimplementation: lazy-union removes the implicit union at TOP LEVEL, so multiple top-level solids export as separate objects (multi-object 3MF) instead of one fused solid; manifold selects the fast geometry backend (semantics-neutral except speed and color-through-render); roof, textmetrics, import-function etc. gate their named features. Unknown flags error.
edge_cases: With lazy-union OFF (baseline), every multi-solid top level is one implicit union — scripts and exporters may silently depend on either behavior.
VERIFY: the full flag list of the targeted snapshot before mirroring; flags come and go between snapshots.
Feature-flag state is not visible from the language (no builtin reports it) — scripts cannot branch on it; only version()/version_num() gate library behavior.
impl_notes: Mirror the mechanism (named opt-in flags) rather than individual flags; implement lazy-union early — it is cheap and unlocks multi-object export.

name: dxf_linear_extrude / dxf_rotate_extrude (deprecated)
signature: dxf_linear_extrude(file, layer, height, ...); dxf_rotate_extrude(file, layer, ...)  // deprecated aliases, functional in 2021.01
summary: Ancient DXF-extrusion modules — still functional in 2021.01 as deprecated aliases of linear_extrude/rotate_extrude with the legacy parameter order.
semantics: These are the same modules as linear_extrude/rotate_extrude reached through their legacy file=/layer= parameters — which is exactly why linear_extrude's true positional order starts (file, layer, height, origin, scale, ...). Calling them works in 2021.01 and emits the DEPRECATED-removal warning; the modern equivalent is an extrusion over a child import().
edge_cases: Emits 'DEPRECATED: The dxf_linear_extrude() module will be removed in future releases. Use linear_extrude() instead.' (and the rotate twin) — VERIFY exact wording per name.
All the classic deprecations — including child() — survived through 2021.01 as deprecated-but-functional builtins; none was removed by the 2021.01 baseline.
impl_notes: Accept as aliases emitting the deprecation warning if strict 2021.01 parity is the goal; recognize-and-hint without executing is a documented divergence.

name: CLI diagnostic switches
summary: Three CLI switches escalate or enable the diagnostic surface; CI users treat them as part of the language contract.
semantics: --hardwarnings promotes every WARNING to a fatal error (exit non-zero at the first one) — the SET of warnings you emit becomes pass/fail behavior. --check-parameters and --check-parameter-ranges (both true/false) control whether builtin-module argument validity and range checks emit their warnings at all — i.e. parts of the warning surface can be switched OFF.
edge_cases: With --hardwarnings, warning ORDER becomes observable (which warning fires first decides the error message).
